TTSMaker supports multiple dialogue blocks, each representing a separate synthesis unit that can use a different language and voice. You can individually adjust the volume, speed, pitch, and other voice settings for each block, giving you full control to match your specific requirements. At the end, TTSMaker converts the text in each block into speech and merges all blocks into a single audio file to create a seamless conversation. 1 Create a dialogue block and enter your text Enter the text you want to convert into speech. Each dialogue block has a limit on the number of characters, so long text must be split into multiple blocks. You can add more blocks to continue the dialogue. 2 Choose the language and AI voice for the dialogue block TTSMaker supports over 100 languages and 600 AI voices. You can select the appropriate language and voice for your text, and customize voice settings such as pauses, volume, speed, pitch, and more. 3 Repeat steps 1–2 to create multiple dialogue blocks Each block can have its own language and voice, and you can adjust its voice settings individually. You can also control the pauses between each block to ensure a natural conversation flow. 4 Generate dialogue audio and download the audio file TTSMaker will generate the voice for each dialogue block and then merge them into a single audio file, ready for download and use. Gaming & Entertainment Content Generate character voices for games and podcasts TTSMaker helps indie developers and creators produce diverse character voices for games, podcasts, and entertainment content without the need for voice actors. FAQs What is TTSMaker AI Voice Dialogue Generator? TTSMaker AI Voice Dialogue Generator lets you generate dialogues with multiple speakers, unlike traditional voice generators that support only one voice. How to increase the number of dialogue blocks? The TTSMaker Free version has a limited number of dialogue generations. Upgrading to TTSMaker Pro allows you to create up to 100 dialogue blocks, unlock higher character limits, and access more advanced features like voice emotion control. How to save dialogue projects? The TTSMaker Free version does not include a save feature. Upgrading to TTSMaker Pro allows you to create and save up to 300 dialogue projects in your account for future use. Can I use dialogues generated by TTSMaker for commercial purposes? Yes! You are free to use the audio files generated by TTSMaker dialogues for commercial purposes without any restrictions. How to use the emotion control feature in voice generation? The TTSMaker Free version does not support emotion control. Upgrading to TTSMaker Pro gives you access to this feature. Voices labeled with the Emotion tag support emotion control, and there are currently around 20 AI voices that support this feature. Does TTSMaker provide customer support? content: 12 Best Audio Transcription Software Picks for 2025Kate StronachSeptember 15, 2025Whether you're a podcaster, journalist, researcher, or marketer, you're likely dealing with a growing mountain of audio and video content. The process of manually transcribing interviews, meetings, and lectures is notoriously slow, costly, and prone to human error. AI-powered tools have solved this bottleneck, but now a new challenge has emerged: a saturated market filled with dozens of options, each claiming to be the best.Why Modern Transcription Tools Stand Out?#1 in speech to text accuracyUltra fast resultsCustom vocabulary support10 hours long fileState-of-the-art AIPowered by OpenAI's Whisper for industry-leading accuracy. Support for custom vocabularies, up to 10 hours long files, and ultra fast results.Import from multiple sourcesImport audio and video files from various sources including direct upload, Google Drive, Dropbox, URLs, Zoom, and more.Export in multiple formatsExport your transcripts in multiple formats including TXT, DOCX, PDF, SRT, and VTT with customizable formatting options.Choosing the right platform is critical, as the best audio transcription software for a solo creator is vastly different from what a corporate legal team needs. Your ideal solution depends entirely on your specific requirements. Are you prioritizing near-perfect accuracy for sensitive legal files, or do you need lightning-fast turnaround for social media content? Is data privacy your top concern, or are seamless integrations with tools like Slack and Zoom more important? Budget, speaker identification, and export formats all play a significant role. This guide cuts through the marketing hype to provide a clear, practical comparison of the top contenders. We'll move beyond generic feature lists to give you a detailed analysis of what works, what doesn't, and who each tool is truly for. We'll examine key factors like accuracy, pricing, security protocols, and unique features to help you make an informed decision.Choosing the Right Tool MattersNot all transcription tools are built the same. Some prioritize accuracy, others focus on integrations or privacy. Understanding the core features you need before comparing platforms ensures you select software that fits your workflow, budget, and long-term goals.For those working with multilingual content, understanding the nuances of turning one language into another is also key; we've created a practical guide on how to translate audio to English that complements the tools discussed here. Our goal is simple: to help you find the perfect transcription software for your specific workflow. Each option reviewed includes screenshots and direct links, so you can evaluate them for yourself. Let's dive in and find the tool that will save you time and transform your audio into actionable text.What Makes a Transcription Tool Stand Out?Accuracy & ReliabilityHigh-quality engines ensure fewer corrections and smoother workflows. Reliable platforms maintain consistent results even with complex audio.Privacy & SecurityTools with strict data protection policies are essential for legal, medical, or corporate recordings. User data must never be used to train external models.Integrations & Workflow FitThe best software blends seamlessly with your existing tools—Zoom, Drive, Slack, or automation workflows—saving time and boosting productivity.Post-Transcription CapabilitiesBeyond basic text output, advanced tools offer summaries, chapters, action items, and repurposing options to maximize value from every recording1. Transcript.LOL Best For: Content Creators and Teams Needing Speed, Accuracy, and Actionable AI Outputs Transcript.LOL positions itself as a powerhouse in the AI transcription space, earning its top spot by combining exceptional accuracy with a suite of intelligent, post-transcription tools. It is an outstanding choice for professionals who need more than just a wall of text. The platform leverages a fine-tuned version of OpenAI’s Whisper, which allows it to deliver transcripts with a cited accuracy rate of ~99.8%, even on complex audio with multiple accents or niche terminology. For those searching for the best audio transcription software, this platform’s core strength lies in its ability to transform a raw recording into a multi-purpose asset. It’s not just about converting speech to text; it’s about making that text immediately useful. This emphasis on workflow efficiency sets it apart from more basic services. Key Features & Analysis AI-Powered Content Generation: Beyond transcription, Transcript.LOL generates summaries, chapters, mind maps, quizzes, and even ready-to-post social media content. This is a game-changer for podcasters and marketers looking to maximize content repurposing from a single audio file. Privacy-First Architecture: In an era of data concerns, Transcript.LOL commits to a strict no-training policy. User audio and transcript data are never used to train AI models, a crucial assurance for users in legal, healthcare, or corporate research fields. Broad Integration & Import Options: The platform supports a vast range of inputs, including local files, Google Drive, Zoom, YouTube links, and direct integrations with WhatsApp and Telegram. An available API and Zapier connection allow it to seamlessly fit into established automated workflows. Team Collaboration: Shared workspaces, folder organization, and global search functionality make it a strong contender for teams. It streamlines the process of managing, reviewing, and collaborating on transcribed content across an organization. Otter.ai Otter.ai has firmly established itself as one of the best audio transcription software options, particularly for those who live in meetings. Its core strength lies in real-time transcription and collaborative features, making it an indispensable tool for teams using platforms like Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams. The OtterPilot™ feature automatically joins your calendar meetings, records audio, takes notes, and even captures slides, delivering a comprehensive summary directly to your inbox. Beyond live meetings, you can upload pre-recorded audio or video files for transcription. The platform excels at speaker identification, automatically labeling different voices to create a clean, readable transcript. Users can then highlight key points, add comments, and assign action items directly within the transcript, turning a simple text file into a collaborative workspace. For those exploring various tools, understanding the nuances between Otter.ai and other free online speech-to-text converters can highlight its meeting-specific advantages. Pricing and Key Features Otter.ai offers a tiered pricing model that includes a free plan. The Basic plan is free but limited, offering 300 monthly transcription minutes with a 30-minute cap per conversation. Paid plans, like Pro and Business, significantly increase these limits and unlock advanced features such as higher-priority processing and enhanced team collaboration tools. Best For: Teams, students, and professionals who need real-time meeting transcription and automated note-taking. Unique Feature: The OtterPilot™ for automated meeting attendance and summarization is a standout feature that streamlines workflows. Pros: Excellent real-time transcription, strong integration with video conferencing tools, and robust collaboration features. Cons: The free tier is quite restrictive, and large file uploads can sometimes face limitations on lower-tier plans. Website: https://otter.ai 3. Descript Descript has revolutionized the content creation space by merging audio transcription with a powerful, text-based audio and video editor. Instead of manipulating waveforms, users can edit their media simply by editing the transcribed text. Deleting a word or sentence in the transcript automatically cuts the corresponding audio or video, making the editing process incredibly intuitive and fast. This unique approach positions Descript as more than just transcription software; it's a complete production suite for creators. The platform is packed with AI-powered features designed to polish content, such as "Studio Sound" for noise reduction and an automatic filler word remover ("uh," "um"). While primarily known for its transcription, Descript is also a robust AI video editing software that can significantly boost your creative workflow. For those who rely on precise timing, understanding how Descript handles transcription with timecodes is crucial for syncing edits with the original media. It also includes screen recording and remote recording via its integrated SquadCast feature, making it a comprehensive tool for podcasters and video producers. Pricing and Key Features Descript's pricing includes a free tier with 1 hour of transcription per month. The Creator plan offers more hours and removes watermarks, while the Pro plan unlocks unlimited transcription and advanced AI features. The Business plan is tailored for teams, adding features like SSO and dedicated support. Best For: Podcasters, video creators, and anyone who needs to edit audio or video content alongside transcribing it. Unique Feature: Text-based "doc-style" editing is its hallmark, allowing users to edit media by editing the transcript text. Pros: Excellent for creators who need integrated editing and publishing features, scales well from individuals to enterprise teams, and offers robust learning resources. Cons: Recent pricing and plan changes can be confusing, and the desktop application is more resource-intensive than simple web-based transcribers. Website: https://www.descript.com/pricing 4. Rev Rev carves out a unique space in the audio transcription software market by offering a hybrid model that combines powerful AI with expert human transcription services. This dual approach makes it a go-to platform for users who need flexibility, allowing them to choose between the speed and affordability of automated transcription for everyday tasks and the near-perfect accuracy of human-powered transcription for critical projects. Rev is particularly well-suited for professional content creators, researchers, and legal experts who cannot compromise on precision. Beyond standard transcription, Rev provides a suite of services including video captioning, subtitling, and an automated meeting notetaker that integrates with Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams. The platform also caters to developers with a robust API for programmatic access to its AI transcription engine, enabling businesses to build speech-to-text functionality directly into their own applications. This comprehensive offering allows users to manage both AI and human-based workflows under a single vendor.Pricing and Key Features Rev’s pricing is transparent, with a clear per-minute rate for human transcription (starting at $1.50/minute) and tiered subscription plans for its AI services. The Rev Max subscription includes an AI meeting assistant and 20 hours of automated transcription per user per year. While the human service is a premium, its quality is an industry benchmark. Best For: Professionals, media companies, and legal experts requiring the highest accuracy, plus businesses needing both AI and human options. Unique Feature: The unified platform for both AI transcription and professional human transcription services is its key differentiator. Pros: Industry-leading accuracy with human transcription, one vendor for both AI and human needs, and strong API for developers. Cons: Human transcription is significantly more expensive than AI-only competitors, and add-ons can increase the total cost substantially. Website: https://www.rev.com/pricing 5. Trint Trint is a powerful, cloud-based platform built for media, legal, and enterprise teams that require more than just a basic transcript. It positions itself as an end-to-end content creation tool, combining highly accurate transcription with a collaborative, in-browser editor. Its standout feature is its ability to handle both pre-recorded files and live audio streams (Trint Live), making it a versatile choice for journalists covering events or legal professionals in depositions. The platform's strength lies in its workflow integration. Users can transcribe, verify, edit, and comment on transcripts with colleagues in real-time. Trint also offers translation into over 70 languages and features AI-powered summaries to quickly extract key insights. This makes it one of the best audio transcription software options for organizations that need to turn spoken words into searchable, editable, and shareable content at scale. The entire process is designed to fit seamlessly into professional media and corporate production pipelines. Pricing and Key Features Trint’s pricing is geared toward professional and enterprise use, with plans structured around user seats and feature sets. While specific pricing often requires a sales consultation, plans like Starter and Advanced offer a set number of transcriptions per user per month. Custom enterprise plans provide API access and enhanced security features for larger organizations. Best For: Journalists, newsrooms, legal teams, and large enterprises needing a collaborative and secure transcription workflow. Unique Feature: The combination of live transcription, a robust collaborative editor, and built-in translation makes it a comprehensive content production tool. Pros: Excellent for team-based workflows, strong feature set tailored to media and legal professionals, and high accuracy across multiple languages. Cons: Pricing can be higher than many competitors and is less transparent, often requiring contact with their sales team for a quote. Website: https://trint.com 6. Sonix Sonix strikes a strong balance between high-accuracy automated transcription, an intuitive feature set, and transparent pricing, making it a powerful contender for one of the best audio transcription software options available. It is particularly well-regarded for its in-browser editor, which allows users to easily review, edit, and polish transcripts alongside the original audio playback. The service excels at speaker diarization and provides word-by-word timestamps, which are invaluable for journalists, podcasters, and video editors who need precise referencing. Beyond standard transcription, Sonix offers automated translation into over 40 languages, a feature that broadens its appeal for global content creators. This combination of transcription and translation within a single workflow simplifies the process of making content accessible to a wider audience. The platform is built for both individual creators and large teams, with API access and enterprise-level security features like SSO available on higher-tier plans. Pricing and Key Features Sonix provides flexible pricing with both a Standard pay-as-you-go option and a Premium subscription. The pay-as-you-go model is prorated by the second, offering excellent transparency, while subscriptions provide lower per-hour rates and additional features for frequent users. A 30-minute free trial allows potential customers to test the service's accuracy and workflow before committing. Best For: Podcasters, journalists, and businesses needing a reliable balance of accuracy, editing tools, and translation capabilities. Unique Feature: The in-browser editor synchronizes text and audio, making transcript correction and verification a seamless process. Pros: Transparent and flexible pricing, a good balance of accuracy and features, and 30 free trial minutes to evaluate the service. Cons: Translation is billed at the same rate as transcription, and advanced security features are gated behind the Enterprise tier. Website: https://sonix.ai/pricing 7. Happy Scribe Happy Scribe carves out a unique space in the audio transcription software market by offering a powerful hybrid model. It combines the speed of AI-powered transcription with the precision of human-led services, giving users the flexibility to choose the right balance of speed, accuracy, and cost for their project. This makes it an excellent choice for creators who need quick, affordable transcripts for some projects and near-perfect accuracy for others, all within one platform. The platform supports an impressive 70+ languages for both transcription and subtitling, making it a go-to for international content. Users can upload files, paste links, or use integrations with tools like Zoom and Google Meet to capture audio. Once transcribed by AI, the interactive editor allows for easy collaboration, speaker identification, and polishing. For those needing maximum precision, upgrading to a human-proofread transcript is a seamless process. Pricing and Key Features Happy Scribe offers straightforward pricing for both its AI and human services. The Basic plan is a free tier for testing the platform with limited credits. The Pro plan provides more monthly transcription hours, while the Business plan adds collaboration tools and custom glossaries. Human-made services are priced per minute, with costs varying by language and turnaround time. Best For: Content creators, marketers, and businesses that require a mix of fast AI and high-accuracy human transcription across multiple languages. Unique Feature: The hybrid model that seamlessly integrates AI and human transcription/subtitling services within a single workflow. Pros: Flexible choice between AI speed and human accuracy, extensive language and subtitle support, and strong collaboration tools for teams. Cons: Human proofreading services can become costly, especially for long-form content or less common languages. Website: https://www.happyscribe.com/pricing 8. Temi Temi distinguishes itself in the audio transcription software market with its straightforward, pay-as-you-go pricing model. This approach is ideal for individuals or small businesses with sporadic transcription needs who want to avoid monthly subscriptions. The service is built for speed and simplicity, offering a reliable automated transcription engine that performs best with clear, high-quality audio recordings free of heavy accents or background noise. It's a go-to solution

In this article, we will delve into the world of Text-to-Speech (TTS) softwares and compare the top five one-time fee options available: Revoicer, Speechelo, Human Talk, Profit Voice, and Mic Monster. We will explore the features, pros and cons of each software, and help you make an informed decision when choosing the right TTS software for your needs. Revoicer Revoicer is a TTS software that offers a standard edition priced at $67, with an additional $197 per year for the Pro version. Let's explore its features: Multiple Voices: Revoicer provides a wide range of voices from different countries, allowing you to give your text a global Flair. Voice Customization: With Revoicer, you have the flexibility to change the tone of certain voices, including the option for whispering. Voice Merging: Merge multiple voice files together seamlessly with Revoicer, giving you more creative control. Music Integration: Revoice or Pro version allows you to add music to the voices, enhancing the overall listening experience. Adjustable Parameters: Customize pauses, speaking rate, and even Translate text within the Pro version of Revoicer. Pros: Wide variety of voices from different countries Voice customization options for added realism Ability to merge voice files and add music Cons: Pro version can be expensive Monthly character limits may be restrictive for some users Speechelo Speechelo is another powerful TTS software that offers a standard version for $27, with a one-time fee of $47 for the Pro upgrade. Let's take a look at its features: Impressive Voice Selection: Speechelo provides 23 voices in the standard version and an additional 50 voices in the Pro version, giving you a wide variety to choose from. Flexible Voice Customization: Adjust pauses, pitch, speed, and even add breathing to create natural-sounding voiceovers. Music Integration: Enhance your voiceovers by adding music to give them a professional touch. Generous Character Limit: Speechelo offers generous character limits, ensuring you have enough room to express your ideas effectively. Pros: Extensive voice selection Versatile voice customization options Music integration for enhanced voiceovers Cons: Inability to merge voiceovers Standard version lacks advanced features available in the Pro version Human Talk If you're looking for TTS software that delivers human-like voices with a touch of emotions, Human Talk might be the perfect choice for you. Here are its key features: Emotional Voices: Human Talk stands out with its 800 voices over 132 languages, and its unique selling point is the ability to add emotions to the voices. AI Content Writer: Enjoy the added benefit of an AI content Writer, providing you with diverse and high-quality content. Versatile Applications: Merge voices into a single file, translate between languages, and take advantage of commercial rights for your projects. Refund Policy: Human Talk offers a 30-day refund policy, giving you peace of mind when purchasing. Pros: Extensive voice library with emotional variety AI content writer for diverse content creation Inclusion of advanced features for translation and voice merging Cons: Higher price compared to other TTS softwares Inability to add music to voices Profit Voice With Profit Voice, you can access a simple yet powerful TTS service at an affordable price. Let's explore its features: Language Variety: Profit Voice offers an extensive range of languages, allowing you to reach a global audience. Customizable Voices: Personalize your voiceovers using emphasis, volume, speed, pitch, and pauses, allowing for natural and engaging audio. Translation Capabilities: Translate Texts seamlessly from one language to another using Profit Voice. Commercial License: Enjoy the freedom to utilize the voices commercially, enhancing your business prospects. Pros: Affordable pricing with a robust feature set Easy-to-use interface for quick voice creation Excellent voice customization options Cons: Limited character limit might restrict longer content Free version has limitations on usage Mic Monster Mic Monster offers a limited free version and a paid version priced at $199. Let's see what it has to offer: Vast Voice Selection: With over 600 voices available across 140 languages, Mic Monster provides an extensive range of voice options. Commercial License: Enjoy the freedom to use the voices commercially, unlocking potential business opportunities. Multi-Voice Conversations: Easily build multi-voice conversations with emotions in a quick and user-friendly interface. Downloadable TTS Voices: With the paid version, you can download your TTS voices for offline use. Pros: Extensive voice library with multiple languages Intuitive interface for effortless voice creation Ability to build multi-voice conversations with emotions Cons: Limited functionality in the free version Relatively higher price compared to other TTS softwares Comparison of TTS Softwares After evaluating the features, pros, and cons of each TTS software, let's summarize the comparison: TTS Software Price Voice Selection Voice Customization Additional Features Revoicer $67-197/yr Wide variety Tone adjustment Voice merging, music Speechelo $27-$47 Extensive Pitch, speed, pauses Music integration Human Talk $297 Emotional variety AI content writer Voice merging, translation Profit Voice <$10 Diverse Emphasis, pitch, etc. Translation capabilities Mic Monster $199 Vast selection Multi-voice conversations Commercial license Conclusion Choosing the right TTS software depends on your specific needs and budget. Revoicer offers multiple voice options and customization features but can be pricey. Speechelo provides an extensive voice library but lacks certain advanced features. Human Talk stands out with its emotional voices, versatile applications, and AI content writer. Profit Voice offers an affordable and powerful TTS service, while Mic Monster provides a quick and user-friendly interface for multi-voice conversations. Consider your requirements and preferences to make an informed decision. FAQs Q: Can Revoicer add music to voiceovers? A: Yes, the Pro version of Revoicer allows you to add music to your voiceovers. Q: Does Human Talk have a refund policy? A: Yes, Human Talk offers a 30-day refund policy for your peace of mind. Q: Can I download TTS voices in Mic Monster's free version? A: The free version of Mic Monster allows you to download your TTS voices for offline use. Q: Can Speechelo merge voiceovers? A: No, Speechelo does not provide the ability to merge voiceovers. Q: Is Profit Voice suitable for commercial use? A: Yes, Profit Voice allows commercial usage with a commercial license. Ledford has been writing, editing, and fact-checking tech stories since 1994. Her work has appeared in Computerworld, PC Magazine, Information Today, and many others. lifewire's editorial guidelines Updated on October 23, 2024 02:28PM EDT We independently evaluate all of our recommendations. If you click on links we provide, we may receive compensation. Otter.ai Software & Apps Mobile Phones Internet & Security Computers & Tablets Smart Life Tech Leaders Home Theater & Entertainment Software & Apps Social Media Streaming Gaming Women in Gaming Now you can get automatic recording and real-time transcription for conversations in English, Spanish, and French. Having a good recording and transcription app on your phone can mean the difference between catching all the details in a conversation and missing something important. That's where Otter.ai comes in, and now it's expanding its capabilities. In a press release sent to Lifewire, Otter.ai announced that it's adding two additional languages to its mobile apps, designed to help you record and transcribe the conversations that matter. The Otter.ai app is available for Android or iOS, and now supports English, French, and Spanish. Users can choose which language they want to use for their default recording and transcription. Unfortunately, Otter.ai won't translate those languages, however, so you'll need to be fluent in whichever language you choose as your default. Otter.ai works both as a mobile app and a web-based app that you can connect to your calendar to record and transcribe virtual meetings on Zoom, Microsoft Teams, or Google Meet. The mobile app can be used for live, in-person conversations, and translations happen in real time as the conversation happens. You can, however, go back and edit the conversation transcription if a mistake appears. The Otter.ai app is free but has several subscription levels. The Basic subscription is free and gives you 300 transcription minutes per month, up to 30 minutes per conversation. For the lifetime of your free subscription, you are limited to importing three audio or video files to transcribe. The Pro subscription is $16.99 per month ($100 when paid annually) and increases your transcription limit to 1200 per month with recordings up to 90 minutes. You'll also be allowed to import up to 10 audio and video files to transcribe per month. There are also Business and Enterprise plans available for anyone who might need more transcription minutes or team support. Sign Up Now How to Use Speech-to-Text on Android Was this page helpful? We use Stripe to securely process payments and we don't store your credit card number. For more security and privacy information, read our Security and Privacy FAQ. Plaud.ai Smart & Connected Life AI & Everyday Life News Byte-Sized Brief Plaud launches a $179 AI-driven note-taker called Note Pro.A "Press to highlight" feature marks key ideas instantly.It supports 50 hours of nonstop recording. Taking notes while staying focused in a meeting can be hard, and even transcription apps can bury the important points. Plaud's new Note Pro is designed to handle both; it records conversations, creates transcripts, and lets you highlight the moments that matter in real time. Plaud already has other note-taking products, like the NotePin, but this one adds a Press to highlight button that lets you instantly mark key ideas so that the AI knows what to prioritize. It's built with four precision microphones that capture audio up to 16 feet away, and it can automatically detect when you're on a call versus an in-person meeting. The battery can handle up to 50 hours of continuous recording, which means most people could get through a full week of work before charging. With the new Plaud App 3.0 update coming later this year, users will also get multimodal inputs, better insights, smarter Ask Plaud features, and a redesigned interface. Pre-orders are open now for $179, with shipping starting in October across the US, UK, and parts of Europe. page_title: Startup's AI app dubs videos in different languages
meta_description: The AI-generated video is in the original speaker's voice. The app also synchronizes lip movements.
content: Skip to main contentOct 10, 2023 - TechnologyStartup's AI app dubs videos in different languagesIna Friedfacebook (opens in new window)twitter (opens in new window)linkedin (opens in new window)email (opens in new window)sms (opens in new window)Add Axios on GoogleAdd Axios as your preferred source tosee more of our stories on Google.Add Axios on GoogleImages courtesy of CaptionsA new free app allows people to get their videos dubbed into any of 28 languages — in their own voice and with their lips synchronized to the translated audio.The big picture: Lipdub, a free iOS app from New York-based AI startup Captions, is the latest demonstration of just how useful generative AI can be — but it also illustrates the technology's immense potential to create realistic looking fakes.How it works: Lipdub requires people to record a video on their phone with only their face in view. The app uploads the video and returns it to the user in a few minutes with the new language overdub applied.For now, Lipdub can handle up to one minute of video from a single speaker.In addition to foreign languages, Lipdub has added options like Texas slang and Gen Z, pirate and baby talk.What they're saying: "Our hope is that the Lipdub technology will remove language barriers and ultimately allow more people to have their stories heard — stories that otherwise might be lost in translation," Captions CEO Gaurav Misra told Axios.Misra said Captions is clearly marking videos made using Lipdub as having been generated with AI.The 25-person startup first created a video studio app that offers automatic captioning using OpenAI's speech-to-text technology. The company says that product has now been used by more than 100,000 people per day to produce more than 2 million videos each month.Between the lines: Misra said the hardest part of creating Lipdub was training its algorithms to mirror natural lip movement while using what are known as "zero-shot" models, meaning they don't need to be trained on an individual speaker. "As you'll notice, the facial expressions of a person remain unchanged pre- and post-translation — only their lip movements change — resulting in a more natural appearance," Misra added. What's next: In the future, Misra says generative AI should allow for real-time translation for broadcasts or video conferencing. "Imagine having a Zoom call with someone who doesn't speak the same language, yet understands you perfectly," Misra said.Go deeper: Watch the demo video, (Really, you should watch it.)facebook (opens in new window)twitter (opens in new window)linkedin (opens in new window)email (opens in new window)sms (opens in new window)Add Axios on GoogleWhat to read nextTechnologyOct 13, 2023Prompt: Using AI to change videos from English to other languagesGo deeper (2 min. read)TechnologyFeb 28, 2024Lightricks' AI movie maker generates entire moviesGo deeper (1 min. read)

MORE OPTIONSAGREEAll PostsFeaturedCarl Franzen January 23, 2026 Credit: VentureBeat made with Flux.2 Pro via Fal.aiDespite lots of hype, "voice AI" has so far largely been a euphemism for a request-response loop. You speak, a cloud server transcribes your words, a language model thinks, and a robotic voice reads the text back. Functional, but not really conversational. That all changed in the past week with a rapid succession of powerful, fast, and more capable voice AI model releases from Nvidia, Inworld, FlashLabs, and Alibaba's Qwen team, combined with a massive talent acquisition and tech licensing deal by Google DeepMind and Hume AI.Now, the industry has effectively solved the four "impossible" problems of voice computing: latency, fluidity, efficiency, and emotion.For enterprise builders, the implications are immediate. We have moved from the era of "chatbots that speak" to the era of "empathetic interfaces." Here is how the landscape has shifted, the specific licensing models for each new tool, and what it means for the next generation of applications.1. The death of latency – no more awkward pausesThe "magic number" in human conversation is roughly 200 milliseconds. That is the typical gap between one person finishing a sentence and another beginning theirs. Anything longer than 500ms feels like a satellite delay; anything over a second breaks the illusion of intelligence entirely.Until now, chaining together ASR (speech recognition), LLMs (intelligence), and TTS (text-to-speech) resulted in latencies of 2–5 seconds.Inworld AI’s release of TTS 1.5 directly attacks this bottleneck. By achieving a P90 latency of under 120ms, Inworld has effectively pushed the technology faster than human perception. For developers building customer service agents or interactive training avatars, this means the "thinking pause" is dead. Crucially, Inworld claims this model achieves "viseme-level synchronization," meaning the lip movements of a digital avatar will match the audio frame-by-frame—a requirement for high-fidelity gaming and VR training.It's vailable via commercial API (pricing tiers based on usage) with a free tier for testing.Inwood TTS-1.5 API cost chart. Credit: InwoodSimultaneously, FlashLabs released Chroma 1.0, an end-to-end model that integrates the listening and speaking phases. By processing audio tokens directly via an interleaved text-audio token schedule (1:2 ratio), the model bypasses the need to convert speech to text and back again. This "streaming architecture" allows the model to generate acoustic codes while it is still generating text, effectively "thinking out loud" in data form before the audio is even synthesized. This one is open source on Hugging Face under the enterprise-friendly, commercially viable Apache 2.0 license. Together, they signal that speed is no longer a differentiator; it is a commodity. If your voice application has a 3-second delay, it is now obsolete. The standard for 2026 is immediate, interruptible response.2. Solving "the robot problem" via full duplexSpeed is useless if the AI is rude. Traditional voice bots are "half-duplex"—like a walkie-talkie, they cannot listen while they are speaking. If you try to interrupt a banking bot to correct a mistake, it keeps talking over you.Nvidia's PersonaPlex, released last week, introduces a 7-billion parameter "full-duplex" model. Built on the Moshi architecture (originally from Kyutai), it uses a dual-stream design: one stream for listening (via the Mimi neural audio codec) and one for speaking (via the Helium language model). This allows the model to update its internal state while the user is speaking, enabling it to handle interruptions gracefully.Crucially, it understands "backchanneling"—the non-verbal "uh-huhs," "rights," and "okays" that humans use to signal active listening without taking the floor. This is a subtle but profound shift for UI design. An AI that can be interrupted allows for efficiency. A customer can cut off a long legal disclaimer by saying, "I got it, move on," and the AI will instantly pivot. This mimics the dynamics of a high-competence human operator.The model weights are released under the Nvidia Open Model License (permissive for commercial use but with attribution/distribution terms), while the code is MIT Licensed.3. High-fidelity compression leads to smaller data footprintsWhile Inworld and Nvidia focused on speed and behavior, open source AI powerhouse Qwen (parent company Alibaba Cloud) quietly solved the bandwidth problem.Earlier today, the team released Qwen3-TTS, featuring a breakthrough 12Hz tokenizer. In plain English, this means the model can represent high-fidelity speech using an incredibly small amount of data—just 12 tokens per second.For comparison, previous state-of-the-art models required significantly higher token rates to maintain audio quality. Qwen’s benchmarks show it outperforming competitors like FireredTTS 2 on key reconstruction metrics (MCD, CER, WER) while using fewer tokens.Benchmark charts for Qwen3-TTS performance compared to other text-to-speech voice AI models. Why does this matter for the enterprise? Cost and scale. A model that requires less data to generate speech is cheaper to run and faster to stream, especially on edge devices or in low-bandwidth environments (like a field technician using a voice assistant on a 4G connection). It turns high-quality voice AI from a server-hogging luxury into a lightweight utility.It's available on Hugging Face now under a permissive Apache 2.0 license, perfect for research and commercial application.4. The missing 'it' factor: emotional intelligencePerhaps the most significant news of the week—and the most complex—is Google DeepMind’s move to license Hume AI’s technology and hire its CEO, Alan Cowen, along with key research staff.While Google integrates this tech into Gemini to power the next generation of consumer assistants, Hume AI itself is pivoting to become the infrastructure backbone for the enterprise. Under new CEO Andrew Ettinger, Hume is doubling down on the thesis that "emotion" is not a UI feature, but a data problem.In an exclusive interview with VentureBeat regarding the transition, Ettinger explained that as voice becomes the primary interface, the current stack is insufficient because it treats all inputs as flat text."I saw firsthand how the frontier labs are using data to drive model accuracy," Ettinger says. "Voice is very clearly emerging as the de facto interface for AI. If you see that happening, you would also conclude that emotional intelligence around that voice is going to be critical—dialects, understanding, reasoning, modulation."The challenge for enterprise builders has been that LLMs are sociopaths by design—they predict the next word, not the emotional state of the user. A healthcare bot that sounds cheerful when a patient reports chronic pain is a liability. A financial bot that sounds bored when a client reports fraud is a churn risk.Ettinger emphasizes that this isn't just about making bots sound nice; it's about competitive advantage. When asked about the increasingly competitive landscape and the role of open source versus proprietary models, Ettinger remained pragmatic. He noted that while open-source models like PersonaPlex are raising the baseline for interaction, the proprietary advantage lies in the data—specifically, the high-quality, emotionally annotated speech data that Hume has spent years collecting."The team at Hume ran headfirst into a problem shared by nearly every team building voice models today: the lack of high-quality, emotionally annotated speech data for post-training," he wrote on LinkedIn. "Solving this required rethinking how audio data is sourced, labeled, and evaluated... This is our advantage. Emotion isn't a feature; it's a foundation."Hume’s models and data infrastructure are available via proprietary enterprise licensing.5. The new enterprise voice AI playbookWith these pieces in place, the "Voice Stack" for 2026 looks radically different.The Brain: An LLM (like Gemini or GPT-4o) provides the reasoning.The Body: Efficient, open-weight models like PersonaPlex (Nvidia), Chroma (FlashLabs), or Qwen3-TTS handle the turn-taking, synthesis, and compression, allowing developers to host their own highly responsive agents.The Soul: Platforms like Hume provide the annotated data and emotional weighting to ensure the AI "reads the room," preventing the reputational damage of a tone-deaf bot.Ettinger claims the market demand for this specific "emotional layer" is exploding beyond just tech assistants."We are seeing that very deeply with the frontier labs, but also in healthcare, education, finance, and manufacturing," Ettinger told me. "As people try to get applications into the hands of thousands of workers across the globe who have complex SKUs... we’re seeing dozens and dozens of use cases by the day."This aligns with his comments on LinkedIn, where he revealed that Hume signed "multiple 8-figure contracts in January alone," validating the thesis that enterprises are willing to pay a premium for AI that doesn't just understand what a customer said, but how they felt.From good enough to actually goodFor years, enterprise voice AI was graded on a curve. If it understood the user’s intent 80% of the time, it was a success.The technologies released this week have removed the technical excuses for bad experiences. Latency is solved. Interruption is solved. Bandwidth is solved. Emotional nuance is solvable."Just like GPUs became foundational for training models," Ettinger wrote on his LinkedIn, "emotional intelligence will be the foundational layer for AI systems that actually serve human well-being."For the CIO or CTO, the message is clear: The friction has been removed from the interface. The only remaining friction is in how quickly organizations can adopt the new stack.MoreA new study reveals that top models like DeepSeek-R1 succeed by simulating internal debates. Here is how enterprises can harness this "society of thought" to build more robust, self-correcting agents.Ben Dickson January 30, 2026 Partner ContentPresented by SAP Jon Dano, SAP January 30, 2026 Credit: VentureBeat made with MidjourneyTwo days after releasing what analysts call the most powerful open-source AI model ever created, researchers from China's Moonshot AI logged onto Reddit to face a restless audience. The Beijing-based startup had reason to show up. Kimi K2.5 had just landed headlines about closing the gap with American AI giants and testing the limits of US. chip export controls. But the developers waiting on r/LocalLLaMA, a forum where engineers trade advice on running powerful language models on everything from a single consumer GPU to a small rack of prosumer hardware, had a different concern.Michael Nuñez January 29, 2026 Credit: VentureBeat made with MidjourneyIn the race to bring artificial intelligence into the enterprise, a small but well-funded startup is making a bold claim: The problem holding back AI adoption in complex industries has never been the models themselves.Michael Nuñez January 27, 2026 Credit: VentureBeat made with MidjourneyChinese company Moonshot AI upgraded its open-sourced Kimi K2 model, transforming it into a coding and vision model with an architecture that supports an agent swarm orchestration. We expect them to book flights, diagnose system outages, manage cloud infrastructure and personalize media streams in real-time.Manoj Yerrasani January 25, 2026 Midjourney/VentureBeatThe modern customer has just one need that matters: Getting the thing they want when they want it. Speech recognition software that integrates with IoT mobile applications lets users control smart devices using voice instructions. As speech recognition solutions become more and more accurate while businesses continue to embrace the IoT, expect to see increased integration between the two within the next five years.Voice-based bots is the next big thing: Another area where speech recognition technology holds promise is chatbots. The findings reveal that Whisper and Gemini are the top performers, while Google consistently ranks last across various conditions.In this article, we will explore the best speech recognition APIs available in 2025, focusing on their accuracy and performance. We will compare offerings from three major cloud providers—AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure—alongside two startups, Assembly AI and Deepgram. Additionally, we will examine the open-source OpenAI Whisper model and the Gemini model, which is a large language model capable of understanding audio. Why Compare Speech Recognition APIs? You might wonder why we need to compare speech recognition APIs when there are numerous benchmarks available. While academic papers often compare models, they typically do not evaluate APIs directly. This is because APIs are black boxes; their internal workings and potential changes are not transparent. For application developers, the goal is to utilize an API without delving into the complexities of model setup. Therefore, a fair comparison of major speech recognition APIs is essential for the developer community. Benchmarking Methodology To conduct a thorough evaluation, I compiled a collection of audio clips that tested various conditions affecting speech recognition, such as noise, accents, and specialized vocabulary. The clips were long enough to assess performance in generating punctuation and capitalization. Here are the conditions tested: Clean English Speech: Audio clips from TED Talks featuring clear speech from native speakers. Noisy Speech: TED Talk clips with added hospital noise to simulate a challenging environment. Accented Speech: Clips from spoken Wikipedia articles read by speakers with Chinese and Indian accents. Specialized Speech: Abstracts from academic papers synthesized into speech using the Eleven Labs text-to-speech system. Each clip was approximately 1 to 2 minutes long, allowing for a comprehensive evaluation of the APIs. The Models and APIs Evaluated Startups Assembly AI: Known for its user-friendly setup and strong performance claims. Deepgram: Similar to Assembly AI, it offers straightforward integration and competitive accuracy. Major Cloud Providers AWS: Offers a robust suite of AI capabilities, including speech-to-text. Google Cloud: Provides speech recognition but has faced criticism for its performance. Microsoft Azure: Another major player with a comprehensive AI offering. Open Source and Large Language Models OpenAI Whisper: An open-source model that can be run locally or in the cloud. Gemini: A multimodal model that supports speech and is capable of converting audio to text. Evaluation Metrics We used Word Error Rate (WER) as the primary metric, which counts the number of insertions, deletions, and substitutions relative to the length of the string. We also considered a normalized version of WER, which removes punctuation and capitalization errors to provide a clearer picture of raw speech-to-text accuracy. Results Overview Clean Speech In the clean speech category, all models performed well, with average WERs below 10%. Whisper emerged as the top performer, followed closely by Deepgram and Gemini. Assembly AI showed similar accuracy but struggled with formatting. Noisy Speech For noisy conditions, most models experienced a slight drop in performance. Whisper, Assembly AI, and AWS handled noise better than Google and Microsoft, which ranked lower in this category. Accented Speech Gemini excelled in recognizing accented speech, outperforming Whisper and Assembly AI. Google's model performed poorly, with a staggering average WER of 35%. Technical Vocabulary In this category, Gemini again took the lead, demonstrating the advantages of large language models in understanding specialized terms. Assembly AI and Whisper also performed well, often achieving lower WERs than in clean speech conditions. Overall Rankings Across all categories, the following rankings emerged: Gemini: Tied for first place, excelling in accents and technical vocabulary. Whisper: Strong performance in clean and noisy speech. Assembly AI: Best for unformatted text but weaker in punctuation. AWS and Deepgram: Solid options, consistently in the middle. Microsoft Azure: Second last, with limited performance. Google Cloud: Consistently ranked last across all tests. Real-Time Streaming Performance When evaluating real-time streaming capabilities, AWS and Assembly AI emerged as the best options, particularly when formatting was not required. All models experienced a drop in performance compared to batch processing, with formatting proving to be a significant challenge. Final Recommendations In conclusion, the best speech recognition APIs for 2025 are: Tied for Best: Gemini and OpenAI Whisper, depending on the specific use case. Runner Up: Assembly AI, particularly strong for unformatted text. Solid Options: AWS and Deepgram, especially for users already integrated into their ecosystems. Avoid: Google Cloud, which has consistently underperformed in all evaluations. This comprehensive analysis highlights the evolving landscape of speech recognition technology and provides valuable insights for developers seeking the most accurate and reliable APIs for their applications.Copy this articleThis article has been created using the same AI that powers Galaxy.ai's YouTube summarizer. content: 7 Best Speech to Text Software Options for 2025 (In-Depth Review)Kate StronachOctober 7, 2025In 2025, the demand for fast, accurate, and intelligent transcription has never been higher. From podcasters and corporate teams to journalists and legal professionals, the right tool can transform hours of audio or video into actionable text, searchable data, and repurposed content. The core challenge is no longer if you can transcribe audio, but how efficiently and effectively you can do it. With so many options on the market, from powerful developer-focused APIs to user-friendly apps, choosing the best speech to text software for your specific workflow can be overwhelming. This guide cuts through the noise. We will dive deep into the top platforms, evaluating them on critical factors like accuracy, speed, unique features, speaker identification, pricing models, and real-world use cases. Our goal is to provide a clear, comprehensive roundup that helps you select a solution that not only transcribes but also accelerates your entire content pipeline. This article moves beyond surface-level descriptions. For each tool, you will find: A detailed review of its core functionality and standout features. Clear pros and cons to help you make an informed decision. Actionable insights on who the software is best suited for. Screenshots and direct links to help you explore further. We’ve done the research to help you find a tool that saves you time, enhances accessibility, and unlocks new value from your spoken-word content. Let’s explore the solutions that are defining the future of transcription. 1. Transcript.LOL Transcript.LOL positions itself as a powerhouse in the competitive landscape of the best speech to text software, offering a comprehensive suite of tools that moves far beyond basic transcription. Built on OpenAI's advanced Whisper engine, it delivers exceptional accuracy and speed, making it an ideal choice for professionals and teams who require more than just a plain text file. The platform is engineered to handle demanding workloads, effortlessly processing audio and video files up to 10 hours long or 5 GB in size, establishing it as a go-to solution for long-form content creators and researchers. What truly sets Transcript.LOL apart is its focus on turning raw transcripts into actionable content. It’s not just about converting audio to text; it’s about what you can do with that text afterward. The platform integrates powerful AI features that automatically generate summaries, chapter breakdowns, action items, and even quizzes from your transcript. This transforms a typically time-consuming post-production task into an automated, efficient workflow, a major advantage for content marketers, podcasters, and corporate teams.Core AI Capabilities That Go Beyond Transcription#1 in speech to text accuracyUltra fast resultsCustom vocabulary support10 hours long fileState-of-the-art AIPowered by OpenAI's Whisper for industry-leading accuracy. Support for custom vocabularies, up to 10 hours long files, and ultra fast results.Import from multiple sourcesImport audio and video files from various sources including direct upload, Google Drive, Dropbox, URLs, Zoom, and more.Editing toolsEdit transcripts with powerful tools including find & replace, speaker assignment, rich text formats, and highlighting.Core Features and Capabilities Transcript.LOL is packed with features designed for both individual power users and collaborative teams: Exceptional Accuracy and Flexibility: Leveraging OpenAI's Whisper, the platform boasts up to 99.8% accuracy. Users can enhance this further with custom vocabulary support for specialized terms, names, or jargon. It accepts a vast array of input sources, including direct uploads, cloud drives (Google Drive, Dropbox), and direct links from platforms like YouTube, Zoom, and Vimeo. AI-Powered Content Generation: This is the platform's standout capability. Beyond transcription, it can produce a variety of AI-generated assets: Summaries & Chapters: Get a concise overview or a detailed breakdown of your content. Social Media Posts: Automatically create ready-to-publish posts for platforms like LinkedIn and X (formerly Twitter). Quizzes & Mind Maps: Excellent for educational content, turning lectures or interviews into learning tools. Chatbot Prompts: Generate reusable prompts for further content exploration with AI. Advanced Editing and Export: The platform features a rich-text editor with speaker detection and labeling, find-and-replace functionality, and easy speaker assignment. When you’re ready, you can export your work in multiple formats, including TXT, DOCX, PDF, and subtitle formats like SRT and VTT. Team-Oriented Workflow: For organizations, Transcript.LOL provides shared workspaces, granular access controls, and robust search capabilities across all team content. Integrations with Zapier and a dedicated API allow it to plug seamlessly into existing enterprise pipelines. The platform operates under a strict no-training policy, guaranteeing that your uploaded files are never used to train AI models. This is a critical assurance for users handling sensitive content in legal, medical, or corporate environments.To help you choose the right approach for your project, here’s a quick breakdown of the most common timestamping methods and where they shine. Each of these methods serves a different purpose, from making a YouTube video more user-friendly to ensuring a legal deposition is accurately documented. Choosing the right one depends entirely on your end goal.Privacy-First Transcription You Can TrustTranscript.LOL follows a strict no-training policy, meaning your audio, video, and transcripts are never used to train AI models. This makes it a reliable choice for sensitive business, legal, and research content. Your data remains private, secure, and fully under your control at all times.The pricing structure is straightforward and provides a clear path for users to scale: PlanPrice (Billed Annually)Key FeaturesBest ForFree Tier$02 transcripts/day, 20-min max upload, low-priority processingTesting the platform or transcribing short clips.Unlimited$120/yearUnlimited transcripts, 10-hour uploads, priority processing, all AI featuresIndividual creators, researchers, and professionals.Team$240/year (for 2 users)All Unlimited features plus shared workspaces and access controlsBusinesses, agencies, and collaborative teams. Final Verdict Transcript.LOL earns its spot as a leading choice for the best speech to text software by successfully bridging the gap between high-accuracy transcription and intelligent content creation. Its ability to handle long files, combined with a privacy-first policy and a powerful suite of AI-driven content repurposing tools, provides immense value. While the free plan is limited, the paid tiers offer an unlimited, high-priority workflow that can save professionals countless hours. If you want a tool that treats transcription as the beginning of your content lifecycle, not the end, Transcript.LOL is an exceptional and well-rounded solution. Pros: High accuracy and speed powered by OpenAI Whisper, with support for very long files. Turns transcripts into usable content like summaries, social posts, and quizzes. Robust team features, integrations, and wide platform import options. Privacy-first approach with a strict no-training policy on user data. Cons: Free plan is limited and best suited for testing purposes. Requires high-quality audio for optimal accuracy, as with any transcription service. Website: https://transcript.lol 2. Nuance Dragon Nuance Dragon stands as a titan in the world of professional dictation, offering a suite of highly accurate, command-driven speech-to-text solutions. For decades, it has been the go-to tool for professionals in demanding fields like law, healthcare, and enterprise who require more than simple transcription. Dragon excels at turning spoken words into text in real-time and allows users to control their entire computer with voice commands, making it one of the best speech to text software options for power users and accessibility. Unlike many modern cloud-only services, Dragon offers a powerful desktop application alongside cloud and mobile versions, giving users flexibility in how they work. This ecosystem approach ensures that whether you're at your desk or on the move, your custom vocabularies and user profiles are synchronized. Key Features and Offerings Dragon's product lineup is tailored to specific professional needs, ensuring users get a tool optimized for their workflow. Custom Vocabularies & Macros: You can train Dragon to recognize industry-specific jargon, acronyms, and names, significantly boosting accuracy. Users can also create voice-activated macros to automate multi-step tasks, such as inserting a boilerplate text block or filling out a form with a single command. Deep Command and Control: Go beyond dictation to fully operate your computer. Launch applications, navigate menus, click buttons, and browse the web entirely hands-free. This is a critical feature for accessibility and productivity. Multiple Product Tiers: Dragon is not a one-size-fits-all solution. It offers Dragon Professional v16 as a perpetual desktop license, Dragon Professional Anywhere as a cloud-based subscription for enterprise, and Dragon Anywhere Mobile for iOS and Android. Who Is It Best For? Nuance Dragon is the ideal choice for professionals who spend a significant portion of their day creating detailed documents and need to maintain high levels of productivity. Legal professionals, physicians, authors, and corporate executives will find its deep customization and hands-free control invaluable. It's also a leading solution for users with physical disabilities who require robust accessibility tools to interact with their computers. Practical Tip: To maximize Dragon's accuracy, spend time in the initial training wizard and use the "Add words to vocabulary" feature early and often. For example, if you are a lawyer, add specific case names, legal precedents, and client names to your custom dictionary before you begin dictating documents. Feature ComparisonDragon Professional (Desktop)Dragon Professional Anywhere (Cloud)PlatformWindows OnlyWindows, Cloud, Mobile AppLicensingPerpetual (One-time fee)Subscription (Annual)Profile ManagementLocalCentralized (Cloud-synced)Best ForIndividuals, small businessesLarge teams, enterprise Pros: Exceptional accuracy with specialized vocabularies. Mature, feature-rich product refined over decades. Powerful hands-free computer control and accessibility features. Cons: Primarily Windows-focused; no modern Mac desktop version. The upfront cost for a perpetual license can be substantial. Website: https://dragon.nuance.com 3. Otter.ai Otter.ai has carved out a unique niche in the speech-to-text landscape by focusing on a specific, high-value problem: transcribing and summarizing meetings and conversations. It transforms live or recorded audio into smart, collaborative notes complete with speaker identification, timestamps, and actionable summaries. This meeting-centric approach makes it one of the best speech to text software solutions for teams, students, and professionals who need to capture and recall conversational intelligence. Unlike general-purpose dictation tools, Otter.ai is designed for collaboration. Its "OtterPilot" can automatically join meetings on Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams, acting as an AI notetaker that allows participants to focus on the discussion rather than on typing. The resulting transcripts are searchable, shareable, and integrated into a team workspace. Key Features and Offerings Otter.ai's platform is built around making meeting content accessible and useful long after the call has ended. Live Transcription and Speaker Identification: Otter transcribes conversations in real time, automatically differentiating between speakers. This is crucial for understanding the context of who said what in multi-person discussions. Automated Meeting Summaries: Using AI, Otter generates a concise summary of the key topics and action items discussed in a meeting. This allows users to quickly grasp the important takeaways without reading the entire transcript. Deep Integrations: The platform seamlessly connects with popular calendar and video conferencing tools. The OtterPilot can auto-join and record scheduled meetings, and users can even use it to capture audio from in-person conversations via the mobile app. Collaborative Workspace: Transcripts can be highlighted, commented on, and shared with team members. This transforms a simple text file into an interactive document for follow-ups and project management. Who Is It Best For? Otter.ai is ideal for corporate teams, project managers, students, journalists, and anyone who regularly participates in meetings. It excels in environments where capturing accurate records of conversations is essential for productivity and accountability. Business professionals can use it to ensure no action item is missed, while students can record lectures for easier review. If your primary need is turning spoken conversations into organized, searchable notes, Otter.ai is a top-tier choice. For a closer look at its capabilities, you can learn more about how Otter.ai functions as an AI note-taker for Zoom. Practical Tip: Before an important meeting, use the "Custom Vocabulary" feature to add names of attendees, project codenames, and specific company jargon. This significantly improves Otter's accuracy and reduces the amount of post-meeting cleanup required on the transcript. Feature ComparisonOtter.ai BusinessOtter.ai EnterpriseTranscription Minutes6000 per user/monthCustomPer-Conversation Limit4 hours4 hoursAdmin & SecurityStandardAdvanced (SAML, SSO)Best ForSmall to medium teamsLarge organizations, regulated industries Pros: Excellent real-time speaker identification. Seamless integration with major video conferencing platforms. Powerful AI-driven summaries and collaborative features. Cons: Primarily focused on meetings; not ideal for general-purpose dictation. Accuracy can be lower in noisy environments or with strong accents. Website: https://otter.ai 4. Microsoft Azure AI Speech Microsoft Azure AI Speech serves as the foundational speech-to-text engine for developers and enterprises building sophisticated voice-enabled applications.Built for Developers, Not End UsersAzure AI Speech is not a plug-and-play transcription app. It is designed for engineering teams who want to embed speech recognition into their own platforms, applications, or workflows. Expect powerful customization, but also a technical setup process.Rather than a standalone app, it's a powerful cloud-based service within the Azure ecosystem, designed for custom integration. This makes it one of the best speech to text software choices for businesses that need to build transcription capabilities directly into their products, workflows, or infrastructure with enterprise-grade security and scalability. Azure AI Speech excels in providing building blocks for transcription, offering both real-time streaming and batch processing for pre-recorded audio files. Its strength lies in its deep customization options and seamless integration with other Azure services, allowing organizations to create highly tailored and secure voice solutions that meet specific compliance and operational needs. Key Features and Offerings Azure AI Speech provides a comprehensive toolkit for developers to embed advanced speech recognition into their applications. Custom Model Training: A standout feature is the ability to create custom speech models. You can upload your own audio data and transcripts to train a model that recognizes unique industry jargon, product names, or accents, significantly improving accuracy for specialized use cases. Diarization & Language ID: The service can automatically distinguish between different speakers in an audio file (diarization) and identify the language being spoken from a wide range of supported languages and dialects. This is essential for transcribing meetings, interviews, and customer service calls. Flexible Deployment Options: While primarily a cloud service, Azure AI Speech can be deployed in containers. This allows organizations in sensitive industries like healthcare or finance to run the transcription models on-premises or at the edge, keeping data within their own network for maximum security and privacy. Who Is It Best For? Microsoft Azure AI Speech is built for developers, large enterprises, and technology companies that require a robust, scalable, and customizable speech-to-text API to integrate into their own software or internal systems. It's ideal for creating voice-controlled applications, building call center analytics tools, or embedding transcription features into media platforms. It is not an out-of-the-box tool for individual end-users but rather a platform for building those tools. Practical Tip: When using Azure AI Speech, start with the base model to gauge its performance. If you encounter accuracy issues with domain-specific terms, use the Custom Speech portal to upload a dataset of text (like product manuals or industry reports) and corresponding audio to fine-tune a model. Text-to-speech (TTS) reads aloud text from documents, PDFs, websites, and books using natural-sounding AI voices. NaturalReader uses Gemini, ChatGPT, and other advanced AI voice models. TTS is helpful for anyone who wants to access written content in an audio format—such as people with dyslexia, students, professionals, language learners, and audiobook listeners. Some of the latest developments in text-to-speech technology include AI Neural TTS, Expressive TTS, and Real-time TTS. What does TTS mean? TTS stands for Text-to-Speech (TTS), also referred to as speech synthesis, a transformative technology that uses artificial intelligence (AI) to convert written text into incredibly lifelike spoken words. TTS systems play a vital role in improving accessibility, particularly for individuals with learning disabilities and visual impairments, as they can have any text read aloud. We've rounded up our five favorite translation apps out of the dozens available. Best for Internet-Free Translation: Microsoft Translator What We Like Languages are free to download for offline use. App is free to use without any subscription required. Connect devices to have conversations inside app. What We Don't Like Camera translation doesn't always detect each word. Some features are not available in all languages. Want to translate text into Klingon? Microsoft Translator can do so. meta_description: If you need to transcribe lectures, voice memos, or just about any kind of audio, here's how to use three popular iPhone apps.
content: ​ GA S REGULAR Mobile Phones > iPhone & iOS > How to Use an iPhone to Transcribe Voice Memos and Lectures Evernote, Rev Voice Recorder, and Aiko are good app options; you can also use Live Captions in Settings > Accessibility By Lisa Mildon Lisa Mildon Lifewire Technology Review Board Member & Quality Team Editor Southern New Hampshire University Lisa Mildon is a Lifewire writer and an IT professional with 30 years of experience. Her writing has appeared in Geekisphere and other publications. lifewire's editorial guidelines Published on September 13, 2024 In This Article View All In This Article Evernote Rev Aiko Live Caption Close What to Know Evernote: Audio > Allow microphone > begin recording > Transcribe.Rev Voice Recorder: + > Record audio > Transcribe.Aiko: Record > Allow microphone > Pause. This article explains a few techniques using three different iPhone applications to transcribe voice memos. We've also included a feature called Live Captions, which debuted in iOS 16. Evernote The popular note organizer app, Evernote, has a lesser-known feature when it comes to transcribing. You can use this app to organize just about everything, but you can also take your iPhone voice memos (or record right from the app) and transcribe them with a single button click. Evernote has a Free version and a Personal subscription. The only real limitation of the free account is the size of the file you upload. Free accounts have a 25MB max size, while the Personal account can have note sizes up to 200MB max. Here’s how to transcribe voice memos (or other audio) in Evernote: Adding a new transcribed recording is basically the same whether you’re creating a new note or adding to an existing one. In Evernote, at the bottom left of your iPhone, tap Create. In the menu that appears, towards the bottom, select Audio. If prompted, choose Allow so that Evernote may use your microphone. Begin recording. You should see a red bar at the top with your recording progress. Tap Stop to end recording. Once your iPhone voice memo appears, select Transcribe. You'll see the transcribed voice memo below the recording. To transcribe a pre-recorded voice memo, ensure your file is in one of the following formats: MP3, MP4, FLAC, and WAV. Evernote doesn't support transcribing the M4A format in the Apple Voice Memo app. Rev: Record & Transcribe Rev: Record & Transcribe is a premium iPhone transcription voice memo app with tons of extra features, including Zoom integration, sharing capabilities, and much more. The audio file should appear in the Recordings screen. Tap Transcribe. On the Transcribe screen, select between Human Transcription or AI Transcription. If you don't have credits loaded, you will get a prompt to Add Credits to complete the transcription. Aiko doesn't work well in the background, so if you receive a call or another app overlays the Aiko interface, it could crash. Open an audio file when you first open Aiko by tapping Open. Alternatively, tap the + (plus sign) and select Import File. Choose the audio file to be transcribed. Aiko will begin transcribing your audio. You may stop it at any time by tapping the Stop button (purple square) at the top right corner. Aiko has a handy Search feature for looking through voice memos transcribed on your iPhone. Just look for the magnifying glass at the bottom of the Aiko interface. content: Skip to main content Plan: Otter Live Notes is a Business feature. Once you have set up Otter Live Notes all Zoom meetings that you host will have automatic live transcription. Your participants, you, and any collaborators can all enjoy the benefits that Live Notes provide during a Zoom meeting. Managing the automatic live transcription Access the live transcript Take notes collaboratively Managing the automatic live transcription You can start, stop, or restart the live transcription at any time. Start the live transcription Start the live transcription If you are using the latest version of Zoom (or any version after 5.6.3), you’ll see new privacy notifications when a meeting is being recorded or live-streamed. Read more about this here. As the host, start the Zoom meeting. A red indicator with the words LIVE will appear in the upper left corner of the Zoom window, indicating that Otter has started live transcribing the meeting. Note: If you do not see the red indicator showing LIVE, please ensure your microphone is not muted. The Live Notes will not begin transcribing until there is audio. Additionally, you can review your setup to ensure your settings are correct. Stop the live transcription Stop the live transcription For portions of the meeting that you do not want to record, you can stop the live transcription. You have 2 ways to stop the live transcription: Expand the Otter.ai (click here to open live transcript) menu and click Stop. Or click the 3 dots More option in the lower right corner of the Zoom controls and click Stop Live Stream. Note: You will not be able to stop the live transcript from Otter's side in the browser when using Live Notes. The live transcript can be stopped through the methods above or when the meeting ends. Restart the live transcription Restart the live transcription Restarting a live transcript will continue transcribing the existing conversation. A new conversation will not be created. Click the 3 dots More option in the lower right corner of the Zoom controls and click Live on Custom Live Streaming Service. The Live Notes will startup and the red LIVE indicator will show again. Access the live transcript All participants will be able to access the live transcript to follow along. Expand the Otter.ai (click here to open live transcript) menu and click the Live on Otter.ai (click here to open live transcript). The live transcript will open in a new browser window. Meeting host Meeting host As the meeting host and owner of the transcript, when clicking Live on Otter.ai (click here to open live transcript), the live transcript will open in Otter, where you can follow along, manage sharing permissions, and utilize Takeaways. Participants of the Zoom meeting Participants of the Zoom meeting Meeting participants will also see the red LIVE transcription indicator in their Zoom window. When participants of the meeting click Live on Otter.ai (click here to open live transcript), the live transcript will open in a new browser window. Meeting participants can follow along, scroll back, or request access to the transcript to collaborate. Collaborate on the live conversation If the owner has already shared the conversation with you, log into the account it was shared with to start collaborating with Takeaways. Collaborators, who are logged into Otter, can highlight, assign action items, leave notes, comment, and add photos that everyone can review. Request access to collaborate To request access, follow the steps below. Click Request access in the playback controls bar. Type in your email. Click Request access. Wait for the owner of the transcript to approve your request. Mobile Otter Live Notes works on the mobile Zoom app as well. Starting a Zoom meeting on your iOS or Android Zoom app, will prompt the live transcript. Both host and meeting participants can open the Otter Live Notes by clicking the Live icon and clicking Live on Custom Live Streaming Services. Known Limitations For participants using Zoom on Chromebook, there is no red LIVE icon. As a workaround, the host can copy the link to Otter Live Notes and paste it into Zoom's chat, so all participants can access it there. Otter Live Notes does not work in breakout rooms. As a workaround, you can utilize OtterPilot to send to a breakout room, or one person in each breakout room can do a side-by-side recording.
