Amazon TranslateMachine translation tools FAQShare Your customers come from different parts of the world, and you may not share the same language. But there’s no reason why this should hold you back from offering the support and service your customers deserve, especially with the advancing technology of machine translation tools. Machine translation tools help you adjust your website, emails, and chats to the language customers understand with real-time translations. So nowadays, you can eliminate every barrier or hesitation preventing your customers from opening up. It lets you offer a great service experience and improve your customer satisfaction score. The translation tools let you attract and retain clients who otherwise wouldn’t do business with foreign companies because of communication gaps. Here are the leading machine translation tools in different categories. Take a quick look and read on to understand why customers like or dislike them. Best machine translation tools at a glance: Best for small businesses: Google Translate Best for mid-market businesses: Google Translate Best for enterprise businesses: Google Translate Highest rated: Translate Me Easiest to use: Google Translate These software solutions are ranked using an algorithm that calculates customer satisfaction and market presence based on reviews from our user community. For more information, please check out our G2 Research Scoring Methodology. Some user reviews may have been edited for clarity. 58.8% of all websites on the internet are in English, and the remaining 41.2% constitute various other languages. What are the best machine translation tools for 2024? Google Translate Microsoft Translator Cloud Translation API Translate Me Rask AI Unbabel Language I/O Conversational Translation Tool Personal Translator Yandex Amazon Translate These are the leading machine translation software solutions from G2’s Winter 2024 Grid® Report. 1. Google Translate Google Translate lets you translate text into 133 languages for free. Google uses neural network learning to compare text from broad sources, making translation better and more contextual. The tool normally translates the text into an intermediary language, such as English, and then into a language you want. Highest-rated features of Google Translate Below are some of the notable features of Google Translate. Direct text translation lets users input text directly into the textbox to translate. Platform support is available on browsers, or you can download it as an application. Document translation allows you to input an entire document’s text for translation. Google Translate pricing Google Translate is free to use. Contact the team for more details on the pricing of advanced features and application programming interfaces (APIs). What users like best: “It can translate any language there is. It can also speak it so you can learn how to pronounce it. It can also give you sentence suggestions and synonyms for the words you're trying to translate and give you other meanings for the word you typed. - Google Translate Review, Adham H. What users dislike: “The user experience (UX) could be slightly better in translating larger or longer documents, which sometimes produces uneven results or does not pick up on formatting versus text.” - Google Translate Review, Alphonse T. Want to learn more about Machine Translation Software? Explore Machine Translation products. 2. Microsoft Translator Microsoft Translator supports text and speech translations through cloud services. As of 2024, it supports 135 different languages and their variations. For less common languages, it’s a suitable machine translation tool. Microsoft Translator doesn’t support Yiddish yet. Highest-rated features of Microsoft Translator Below are some of the notable features of Microsoft Translator. Auto-detect language automatically recognizes the language of the input. Real-time translation makes translated text available to you as you type. Image translation recognizes text in an image and translates it into the required language. Microsoft Translator pricing Microsoft Translator offers a free plan. You can contact them for more details on advanced features pricing. What users like best: “​​Microsoft Translator is a great application that can translate various languages, writings, and pictures into our native language. Since I work in a fashion publishing company, I have to travel extensively to cover the stories of unheard-of arts and cultures. With Microsoft Translator, it becomes easier to understand their languages and have a good talk. Its live translation is amazing. I am a very frequent user of this app for my work purposes.” - Microsoft Translator Review, Shubhangi K. What users dislike: “One problem I found with frequent traveling is that since it's cloud-based software, it does not work when I don't have internet. Users of less common language pairs may find the translation quality less reliable. - Yandex Review, Panagiotis G. 10. Cross-lingual communication adds translation to chat, email, helpdesk, and other software to eliminate communication barriers. Amazon Translate pricing Below are some noteworthy details on Amazon Translate’s pricing. A free tier is available. Standard text translation starts at $15 per 1 million characters. One final thing I love about Amazon Translate is it can process various file formats.” - Amazon Translate Review, Akarsh S. What users dislike: “It's hard to tag the cost when multiple services use it.” - Amazon Translate Review, Lezgin B. Machine translation tools FAQ Several questions come up in the quest for your perfect translation tool. Get answers to the most prominent ones. What is a machine translation tool? A machine translation tool uses AI to contextually translate text in different languages without human involvement. The translation goes beyond one-word to one-word substitution; the software understands the entire meaning of the original text and looks at every part of it to keep the context the same in the translated language. What are the three main techniques used for machine translation? Machine translation comes in three main types, each using different methods to translate text. Rule-based machine translation (RBMT) uses expert-crafted rules and dictionaries to translate. It adds knowledge about grammar, word forms, and meanings into the translation. Although it works for languages with fewer resources, it can take a lot of information to create and update rules. Statistical machine translation (SMT) uses statistical models trained on texts in the original and target languages. It finds patterns and connections between the two languages through phrase-based SMT and syntax-based SMT. Phrase-based SMT translates words or phrases to understand the context better and improve the translation. Syntax-based SMT follows grammar rules to keep the structure of the original text. Best AI Summarizers (2026) Why You Can Trust Cybernews Being behind major reports like The Mother of All Breaches and RockYou2024, our in-house cybersecurity experts and journalists provide unbiased, real-world testing and in-depth analysis. We maintain complete transparency by openly sharing our testing methodologies with our audience. Learn more Last updated: 3 December 2025 Mirza Silajdzic Business Tech & AI Solutions Expert The rise of AI has brought about some useful tools, and document summarizers truly stand out among the best. They can transform long, dense content into easy-to-digest summaries, streamlining your workflow and freeing up your time for other important tasks. Of course, these advantages only come with the best summary generator software solutions. To ensure you don’t waste time on subpar options, Cybernews tech experts and I have done the research on your behalf. In this article, we share our findings – the best AI summarizer list, along with comprehensive reviews and analysis of these tools’ functionality, strengths and weaknesses, and features. Top 10 AI summarizers shortlist Jasper AI – best customization capabilities Quillbot – ideal for crafting short-form summaries Canva – best for visually polished summaries Notta AI – excellent audio transcriber Writesonic – top PDF summarizer AI tool ChatGPT – great choice for article summaries HubSpot – leading meeting summarizer AI software ClickUp – easy pick for users seeking to boost their productivity Scribbr – go-to AI summarizer for beginners and minimalists Eightify – best YouTube video summarizer Scholarcy – popular choice among students and researchers What features should I look for in an AI summarizer?Summarizing AI tools must offer a particular set of features to provide real value. I’ve listed the essential ones you should look for in your tool. Ticking all the boxes might be a challenge, but the closer you come to it, the better summaries you can expect. Accuracy: Your AI summarizer should be able to recognize the main points in any text, no matter how long or complex. It should deliver a clear, concise summary to help you make informed decisions without the extra effort. Flexibility: The best AI summarizing tools allow you to fine-tune the length and focus of the summaries. For example, you might need a detailed overview for a research paper but only a quick recap for an email thread. Compatibility: When dealing with various documents, you'll want a summary AI tool that offers multi-format support. It should handle PDFs, .docs, OCR, .rfts, multimedia, and other formats with the same level of accuracy and precision. Multi-language support: Your AI summary generator should handle multiple languages seamlessly. It shouldn’t matter if it's summarizing an English legal document or a German financial report – you must trust it’ll deliver consistent and reliable output every time. User-friendly design: Your AI tool should have a simple interface with little to no learning curve to meet your needs. Its job is to save you time, so you shouldn’t have to deal with complex settings or reconfigurations. Best 10 AI summarizers reviewedNow that you have all the basics down, it’s time to jump into the best AI summarizer reviews. Check out what the Crypronews team and I have uncovered about each one to help you make an informed decision. 1. Jasper AI: best AI summarizer for customized output Best for:Customized outputStarting price:$59.00/monthFree version:YesTop features:Brand style, voice, and audience-tailored content, 30 languages supported, multi-format compatibility Visit Jasper AI Jasper AI is a content generator that features an AI text summarizer. While this is only one of the many tools it offers, it’s impressively versatile. It can handle 30 languages and many different document formats, including text, video, and audio. Yet, it doesn’t take more than a couple of clicks to receive a command and complete the task. What really stood out to me the most was Jasper’s customization options. It can reflect your brand’s voice and style while tailoring its tone to cater to a specific target audience. Plus, it responds well to custom prompts, allowing you to fine-tune the output without much effort. These benefits make it particularly popular with marketers and content creators. Pros Reputable brand Versatile AI toolkit Voice, tone, and demographic-geared customization Diverse format compatibility 30-language support Quick processing Cons Pricey plans 2. Quillbot: best for short-form summaries Best for:Short-form summariesStarting price:$8.33/monthFree version:YesTop features:User-friendly interface, adjustable paragraph and key-point summaries, free 1,200-word coverage Visit Quillbot Quillbot is a powerful, user-friendly summarizing AI tool. With just one click, it can condense text into either paragraphs or bullet points. It also lets you adjust the summary length with a slider, check for plagiarism, and highlight keywords. Now, it doesn’t cover video and audio files and might not work as well for lengthy articles and documents. However, its short-form essay, journal, and email summaries get the point across without the need for complicated configuration or costly subscriptions. Quillbot handles up to 1,200 words for free and up to 6,000 for only $8.33/month in over 45 languages. These capabilities make it perfect for beginners and an excellent option for students. Pros Easy-to-use tool Paragraph and bullet-point output Slider-based length customization Up to 1,200 words for free 45+ languages supported Cons No audio or video file support Limited capabilities with lengthy text 3. Canva: best for designing shareable summaries Best for:Designing eye-catching, shareable summariesStarting price:$0.00/monthFree version:YesTop features:Free AI text summarizer, polished visual layouts, seamless export and sharing Visit Canva Summarizer Canva’s AI summarizer uses OpenAI technology within its editor to quickly generate shareable overviews from lengthy content, making it easy to create presentable summaries. Beyond shortening text, Magic Write extracts key points and action items, helping turn rough, disorganized content into clear, skimmable summaries. After you have your draft summary, you can adjust fonts, colors, and layout, add titles and bylines, include links to the full piece, and create banners or visuals. This way, your final result looks like a polished social post, handout, or slide instead of a basic AI draft. If you already use Canva for content creation, the summarizer fits easily into your usual workflow. Basic text summarization is free in the browser. For more advanced AI features and higher limits, Canva’s premium Magic Studio is available. This upgrade may be helpful if you often use AI for writing, design, or data summaries in Canva Sheets. Pros Free browser-based summarizer Strong visual customization Easy publishing and sharing Integrated with Canva workspace Good at extracting key points Cons Advanced AI features behind paywall Limited controls for deep research use May need tweaks for very technical topics 4. Notta AI: best for summarizing audio files Best for:Summarizing audio filesStarting price:$4.99/monthFree version:YesTop features:Handles a variety of content with ease, includes timestamps, offers convenient editing tools Visit Notta AI Notta Ai is a robust AI tool designed for transcription. It leverages sophisticated automatic speech recognition (ASR) technology to work with various audio and video files with precision and consistency. It easily covers a range of content – from conversational podcasts and interviews to lengthy meetings and videos with technical jargon. There is room for improvement in terms of managing heavy accents and customizing summary length. But its timestamp and editing features impressed both me and my team. They make referencing the original file and adjusting the transcripts straightforward and fast. Notta AI offers these types of perks at just $4.99/month, which makes it one of the most affordable options among the best AI text summarizer software solutions we reviewed. Pros Precise audio and video transcriptions Versatile content compatibility Easy-to-reference outputs Solid editing features Low monthly fee Cons No length-adjustment tools Occasional accent-associated errors Limited features in the free plan 5. Writesonic: best AI PDF summarizer Best for:PDF summarizingStarting price:$0.00/monthFree version:YesTop features:Great long-form text processing, effective ad hook and SEO features, flexible range of pricing plans Visit Writesonic Writesonic is a multi-functional AI tool with impressive PDF summarization abilities. It handles lengthy documents effortlessly, delivering clear, to-the-point summaries. It also makes tailoring output simple thanks to different voice options, compelling hook creation, and SEO tools. Such features are an excellent match for advertisers seeking an easy, quick, and cost-effective way to craft content that boosts online visibility. Writesonic’s concise summaries make excellent ad copies for social media and e-commerce. The pricing plans, including a free option, also make budgeting simple. My main issue is the way its features are divided across plans and its somewhat cluttered interface. Compared to other tools, Writesonic is not as beginner-friendly and suitable for those looking for a streamlined experience. Pros Quality PDF-based output Strong content and SEO enhancement options Several tone customization options Wide range of pricing plans Cons Poor feature selection per plan Fairly overwhelming design Occasional proofing and fact-checking needed 6. ChatGPT: best AI article summarizer Best for:AI article summariesStarting price:$20/monthFree version:YesTop features:Quick and responsive, adaptable to various topics and content requests, backed by up-to-date Google search Visit ChatGPT ChatGPT is by far the most well-known AI tool on our list, so it hardly needs an introduction. While it offers a wide range of features, we found it to be the best AI to summarize articles. The famous tool easily processes long web-sourced texts from various fields, adapting its output to fit different needs and audiences. Thanks to its access to Google search, it also easily fills in the gaps, adding relevant information or refining the language. Its biggest weakness, however, lies in formats beyond plain text. Without access to web data, ChatGPT may struggle with audio or video as well as less common text files. Some users complain about its tendency to produce summaries that are generic, repetitive, or lacking in substance. Pros Offers a rich feature lineup Adapts tone and style to fit various needs Enhances summaries with Google search integration Remains quick and efficient with prompts Cons Struggles with non-text content formats May offer repetitive or redundant output Tends to oversimplify technical jargon 7. HubSpot: best for meeting summaries Best for:Meeting summarizingStarting price:$15.00/monthFree version:YesTop features:Live meeting recording, transcription, and summarization, easy integration capabilities, free to use Visit HubSpot HubSpot is another AI tool with a range of functions. Yet, I’ve chosen it primarily for its Fathom AI Notetaker. It’s a HubSpot-certified app that can record, transcribe, and summarize your online meetings in real time, whether they’re in audio or video form. It syncs flawlessly with multiple popular meeting and communication platforms. Whether your company uses Microsoft Teams or Google Meet or communicates through Slack or Zapier, HubSpot’s summarizer will capture all the key moments and help you share them with your colleagues. Still, a few limitations hold it back. The app can’t handle standalone audio or video files, so it’s ineffective for in-person meetings. It also lacks templates, which would give you a little more control over your summaries’ structure. Pros Real-time recording, transcription, and summarization Popular platform-compatibility Easy-to-use interface Free-of-charge app Cons Not compatible with standard audio and video files Lacks meeting templates Limited language support 8. ClickUp: best for productivity optimization Best for:Productivity optimizationStarting price:$10.00/month (per user)Free version:YesTop features:Instant task, report, and document synopses, auto-generating summarizer capabilities, real-time summary notifications Visit ClickUp AI ClickUp AI is just one feature of the namesake project management tool made for work optimization. True to its name, the tool offers task, report, note, and document summaries with a click of a button. Now, its output can feel robotic and generic, with little leeway for refining, so it’s not best for creative fields. However, it delivers clear and concise updates. The Cybernews team and I particularly liked its auto-summary capabilities. You can use it to set up summary blocks in shared documents across multiple languages. It can also send automatic notifications with comment and message thread summaries straight to your phone. It’s an easy way to keep your team coordinated no matter where they are working. Pros Built to boost productivity Responsive to different content Great for auto-generated summaries Capable of sending notifications to your phone Cons Prone to producing generic output Poor at regenerating based on conversational prompts Expensive due to per-user charges 9. Scribbr: best for simplicity and ease of use Best for:Simplicity and ease of useStarting price:FreeFree version:YesTop features:Minimalistic design, solid complex language command, fully mobile and desktop compatible and free Visit Scribbr Scribbr is an AI platform built for scholars and researchers. It offers tools like proofreading, plagiarism checking, and a simple yet effective text summarizer. Its design is clean and intuitive, comparable to Quillbot’s. Open it, and you’ll find two empty fields – input and output – along with a length slider and two output formats – paragraph or bullet points. This makes it the easiest AI document summarizer to use on this list. However, its simplicity comes with some drawbacks. You can’t summarize more than 600 words at once, forcing you to split long content into sections. It also offers only auto-generated keyword customization, so you won’t be able to refine your summaries with prompts. Pros Intuitive and user-friendly Decent command over complex language Free to use on desktop and mobile Cons Covers up to 600 words at once Offers poor customization features Has only one pricing plan 10. Eightify: best for YouTube video summaries Best for:YouTube video summariesStarting price:$9.99/monthFree version:No (only a 7-day free trial)Top features:Time-stamped video-to-text transcription, easy-to-share key insights, comprehensive top-comment overviews Visit Eightify Eightify is an AI tool built specifically for YouTube content. While its niche focus limits its use elsewhere (not even other video platforms), you’re bound to find its versatility impressive within its domain. The software doesn’t only transcribe and condense content available on YouTube. It can interpret video files in more than 40 languages and across a range of topics while organizing this information in multiple ways. For instance, it gathers key insights, adds timestamps according to tackled topics, and breaks down other viewers' feedback on the video. Eightify also lets you share your summaries with your friends or co-workers through easily accessible links. It also works seamlessly on mobile devices through its standalone apps. I only wish it wasn’t as dependent on internet connectivity – it’s not the best fit for low-bandwidth areas. Pros Quick and easy YouTube video summaries Topic-related timestamp references Well-designed standalone mobile apps Cons Only applicable to YouTube videos Highly dependent on internet connection 7-day free trial 11. Scholarcy: best for students and researchers Best for:Students and researchesStarting price:$4.99/monthFree version:YesTop features:Diverse academic content coverage, learning style and needs-geared output, versatile export options Visit Scholarcy Much like Scribbr, Scholarcy is an AI summarizer designed to assist learning. Yet, I found it to be much more popular among students and researchers because of its robust set of features. It quickly scans and summarizes research papers, reports, and even book chapters. The output adapts to your reading style – you can get highlighted key terms for reference, bulleted lists for quick skimming, or flashcards for easier memorization. Scholarcy also allows you to adjust the language to your student level and export its output to various platforms. But it has trouble with multimedia-heavy text and doesn’t always import smoothly. Plus, its best features are locked behind its pro plan. What Can It Do? Close What to Know Automatic transcription: Give OtterPilot calendar access to record and transcribe every meeting.Manual recording: Select Record to transcribe in real-time, or copy a meeting link in the Paste URL to record box. Upload: Click Import or drag and drop file > view progress bar > locate completed transcription in My Conversations. This article explains how to use Otter AI to transcribe meetings using OtterPilot for automatic or manual recordings or audio file uploads. How to Transcribe With Otter AI Otter AI offers multiple methods for audio transcription, including: Real-time participation as a meeting “participant” and notetaker. Manually recording a meetingUploading audio or video files These steps outline each of these methods. The screenshots and instructions focus on the web interface, but the steps are largely the same in the mobile app. Automatically Transcribe Meetings With OtterPilot Sign up for an account at Otter.ai and verify your email address. Once you’ve confirmed your account and logged in, select Apps in the left sidebar. To link a calendar, choose Add beside your desired option. You can repeat these steps to link multiple calendars. Sign in to your calendar account if prompted and confirm the account link-up by selecting Yes or Allow. View and edit the meetings OtterPilot will attend by returning to your account Home page and selecting a day from the calendar view. Use the toggle feature to allow or restrict OtterPilot’s access. Once Otter AI finishes processing the conversation, view the transcript in My Conversations. You can also link your Zoom account and meeting schedule from Apps > Zoom > Add. OtterPilot will automatically join all meetings you host and record, unless you toggle off access. Manually Record and Transcribe Meetings With OtterPilot If you’d rather not provide calendar access to OtterPilot, you can also manually record and transcribe meetings using these steps: On your account Home page, find the Paste meeting URL to record box in the upper-right corner. Copy and paste a Zoom meeting URL and press Enter on your keyboard. In your active Zoom meeting, press Allow in the dialog box that appears to confirm OtterPilot’s note-taking permissions. Alternatively, in a non-Zoom or Teams meeting, you can manually record a conversation or meeting using the Record button in the upper-right corner of your Otter AI home page. Transcription happens in real-time and appears in the Summary view. Find the completed conversation from the My Conversations or All Conversations tabs. Upload Meeting Recordings If you have a meeting recording you’d like to process and transcribe, you can upload it to Otter AI. From your Otter AI Home screen, look for the Import button in the upper-right corner. Select Browse files or drag and drop the file to upload. Compatible file types include audio and video formats, such as AVI, MP4, MOV, MP3, WAV, and AAC. Double-check the compatibility list and make sure it doesn’t exceed 5GB before uploading. The upload progress bar appears on screen. Once processing completes, view the fully transcribed conversation from the My Conversations tab What Is Otter AI? Otter AI is a meeting and transcription service that uses the OtterPilot AI assistant to automate note-taking. It can use real-time recordings, uploaded audio or video files, or join active meetings to capture and transcribe conversations live. Otter AI offers the ability to record and share transcription summaries with team members using the web and mobile apps and integrates with various services including Slack, Google Calendar, Zoom, and Microsoft Teams. It’s available with a free account tier, but the paid memberships provide fewer limitations on the number of transcription minutes, audio and video file imports, and more. What Can Otter AI Do? Otter AI bundles several core features using two main AI tools, OtterPilot and AI Chat. Here are some of the most noteworthy features of both tools and the platform as a whole. OtterPilot: OtterPilot is the AI meeting assistant that joins meetings automatically (or when prompted) and provides live transcription. OtterPilot also lets users add slides directly from live recordings for easy reference; turn this setting on from Account Settings > Meetings > Auto-capture meeting screens.Otter AI Chat: Ask Otter Chat to help you summarize the main points of a meeting and distill it into an email for colleagues. You can also ask follow-up questions, gather meeting minutes to distribute, or enable Otter Chat Q&A for live question fielding (and answering) during meetings.Organize chats: You can create folders to categorize recordings and transcripts from the Folder area in your Otter AI account. Users can share folder content with teammates in channels, which can serve as a central repository for transcripts and chats.Otter Workspaces: This enterprise-level of access creates spaces for teams to collaborate using all of the transcription and organizational tools. content: Using Language Interpretation in your meeting or webinar Using Language Interpretation in your meeting or webinar English (Original) English (Original)DeutschEspañolFrançaisBahasa IndonesiaItaliano日本語한국어NederlandsPortuguês (Brasil)PolskiРусскийSvenskaTürkçeTiếng Việt中文繁體中文 This article was updated • 2025-10-20 Copy Permalink In this article Requirements and limitationsHow to set up language interpretation for meetings or webinars Add interpreters to a webinar How to start Language Interpretation in meetings or webinarsHow to manage your language interpreter role Switch audio channels as an interpreter and use interpretation relay How to listen to Language Interpretation Host can designate up to 20 participants as language interpreters for a Zoom meeting or webinar. When the meeting or webinar starts, the host can start the interpretation feature which will allow the interpreters to provide their own audio channels for the language they are translating to. Attendees can then select the audio channel to hear the translated audio in their language of choice, as well as the option to mute the original audio instead of hearing it at a lower volume in their chosen language. Cloud recordings of interpretation sessions will record the original audio of the meeting or webinar, as well as the translations. Local recordings of interpretation sessions will record any audio the person recording can hear, but not multiple audio channels. Notes: For webinars, whomever you assign to be a language interpreter is also automatically made a panelist.When using language interpretation and sharing your screen with computer audio, all participants will hear your audio at 100%. To prevent audio imbalance, it is recommended to avoid sharing audio while language interpretation is active.To add language interpretation to a recurring meeting or webinar, after clicking Edit, click All to add language interpretation to all occurrences. Requirements for using Language Interpretation Pro, Business, Education, or Enterprise accountLanguage Interpretation enabledMeeting with an automatically generated meeting IDZoom desktop app for Windows or macOS: Global minimum version or higherZoom mobile app for Android or iOS: Global minimum version or higherZoom web app Limitations of language interpretation Language interpretation can’t be used in meetings using a Personal Meeting ID (PMI). To enable language interpretation, choose the option Generate Automatically for the Meeting ID. You must enable language interpretation for a scheduled meeting or webinar. You can’t add or start language interpretation for instant meetings.Language interpretation can’t be initiated or managed when using the Zoom mobile app or web app. Participants joining from the Zoom mobile app or web app can only listen to interpretation audio channels and view interpreted text.Language interpretation can’t be used in breakout rooms, only the main session of a meeting. Show more How to set up language interpretation for meetings or webinars Add interpreters to a meeting Sign in to the Zoom web portal.In the navigation menu, click Meetings.Click Schedule a Meeting.Next to Meeting ID, select Generate Automatically. This setting is required for language interpretation. Next to Interpretation, select the Enable language interpretation check box.Note: If you previously selected the Enable language interpretation by default check box at the account, group, or user level, this check box will already be selected and enabled as a default setting for all scheduled meetings.Enter the information for your interpreters.The languages you select for interpreters will create audio channels for those languages in your meeting, but not all of these channels have to be used in the meeting.Note: The pre-assigned interpreters must be signed in to the account associated with the chosen email address. If they are not signed in with that email address when joining the meeting or webinar, they will not be recognized as an interpreter; however, the host can manually assign them to be the interpreter in the meeting. Click Save.(Optional) To modify the list of interpreters, click Edit. To add additional interpreters, click + Add Interpreter. Then, enter the information for your interpreters. To resend email invitations, click the email icon next to the interpreter's name.To copy email invitations, click the ellipses next to the interpreter's name . Then, click Copy Invitation.To remove interpreters. click the ellipses next to the interpreter's name . Then, click Remove This Interpreter. Click Save when you are finished. Add interpreters to a webinar Sign in to the Zoom web portal.In the navigation menu, click Webinars.Click Schedule a Webinar or hover over an existing webinar and click Edit.Next to Interpretation, select the Enable language interpretation check box.Note: If you previously selected the Enable language interpretation by default check box at the account, group, or user level, this check box will already be selected and enabled as a default setting for all scheduled webinars.Enter the email address and language information for your interpreters.The languages you select for interpreters will create audio channels for those languages in your webinar, but not all of these channels have to be used in the webinar.Note: The pre-assigned interpreters must be signed in to the account associated with the chosen email address. If they are not signed in with that email address when joining the webinar, they will not be recognized as an interpreter; however, the host can manually assign them to be the interpreter in the webinar. Click Schedule or Save.(Optional) To modify the list of interpreters, click Edit. To add additional interpreters, click Add Language Interpreter. Then, enter the information for your interpreters. To resend email invitations, click the email icon next to the interpreter's name.To copy email invitations, click the ellipses next to the interpreter's name , then click Copy Invitation.To remove interpreters, click the ellipses next to the interpreter's name , click Remove This Interpreter. Click Save when you are finished. How to start Language Interpretation in meetings or webinars Note: Language interpretation cannot be initiated or managed when using the Zoom mobile app. Participants joining from the Zoom mobile app can only listen to interpretation audio channels and view interpreted text. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.Start or join a meeting or webinar.Once your meeting has started, in the controls toolbar, click Interpretation .Note: If you do not see Interpretation, click More .You can add or remove interpreters from this menu if necessary.Click Start to begin the interpretation sessions.After the host clicks Start, the interpreters will receive a message that they have been assigned a language.Note: The pre-assigned interpreters must be signed in to the account associated with the chosen email address. If they are not signed in with that email address when joining the session, they will not be recognized as an interpreter; the host however can manually assign them to be the interpreter in the meeting.Interpreters and attendees can now click Interpretation in the meeting controls and select a language channel.An interpreter in the channel will hear the original meeting audio which they can translate. Interpreters only have access to the language channel they have been assigned to. Participants in a language channel will hear the translated audio and also the original audio at a lower volume.Note: The original audio volume will return to 100% 8 seconds after an interpreter has stopped speaking.To end the interpretation session(s), the host must click Interpretation in the meeting controls.Once the Language Interpretation window opens, the host can click End to stop the sessions.(Optional) The host can also click Manage Language Interpretation to make changes to the interpreter settings during a session. How to manage your language interpreter role As a language interpreter, you can only broadcast to one language channel at a time. This eliminates unnecessary language crossover and helps reduce confusion. You can switch between the native audio channel of the meeting and the interpretation audio channel you have been assigned to. Note: You can only join language interpretation from computer audio. You cannot use the dial-in or call me phone audio features. Once a meeting host assigns you as a language interpreter, a window will appear, notifying you of which language you are responsible for: Sign in to Zoom desktop app.Join a meeting that you have been assigned as an interpreter by the host.Click OK to accept the language you have been assigned to interpret. Switch audio channels as an interpreter and use interpretation relay To switch between audio channels during the meeting: Click the language of the audio channel you want to broadcast to.Speak in the language of the audio channel you are broadcasting to. As an interpreter, you are listening to the main audio channel by default, but you can change the audio channel to listen to another interpreter. This is known as an interpretation relay. This is useful when you don't understand the main language channel and need to interpret from another available language. For example, you may not understand the English spoken in the main channel, but do understand French. You can instead listen to the French interpretation channel and translate that into the language you were assigned to interpret for. To change your incoming audio feed to another language interpretation channel: Next to Listening in, click the drop-down menu. Select the audio channel you want to listen to. By default, Main audio is selected. How to listen to Language Interpretation Windows | macOS | Web appAndroid | iOS In your meeting/webinar controls, click Interpretation . Click the language that you would like to hear.(Optional) To hear the interpreted language only, click Mute Original Audio. Notes: You must join the meeting audio through your computer audio/VoIP. You cannot listen to language interpretation if you use the dial-in or call me phone audio features.As a participant joining a language channel, you can broadcast back into the main audio channel if you unmute your audio and speak. In your meeting controls, tap the ellipses .Tap Language Interpretation. Tap the language you want to hear.(Optional) Tap the toggle to Mute Original Audio.Click Done. Notes: You cannot listen to language interpretation if you use the dial-in or call me phone audio features.As a participant joining a language channel, you can broadcast back into the main audio channel if you unmute your audio and speak. New York, NY; 13 May 2025 – KUDO, the world’s leader in multilingual meeting solutions powered by professional interpreters and AI, today announced the release of AI Assist—a first-of-its-kind feature offering real-time speech transcription to interpreters directly within the KUDO interpreter console. This innovative capability is available immediately at no additional cost to all users of the KUDO multilingual platform. AI Assist represents a major leap forward in interpreter support technology, delivering live captions of the speaker’s language to help interpreters maintain precision, confidence, and cognitive endurance during even the most complex meetings. “This isn’t just another feature; it’s a breakthrough in how we support the incredible professionals who carry the weight of multilingual communication on their shoulders,” said Fardad Zabetian, CEO of KUDO. “With AI Assist, we’re combining the best of speech technology and interpreter-first design to redefine what’s possible in real-time language access.” Real-Time Intelligence in the Booth KUDO’s AI Assist provides interpreters with fast, accurate, real-time transcription of the original spoken language—right as it happens. This in-booth companion helps interpreters: Confirm numbers, acronyms, and specialized terminology with confidence Quickly recover missed words or unclear moments Reduce cognitive load in high-pressure interpreting environments Built specifically for simultaneous interpretation, KUDO’s transcription engine offers: Ultra-low latency, with no distracting flickering or post-processing corrections Exceptionally low Word Error Rate (WER), setting a new market benchmark A clean, flexible interface that integrates into the interpreter console or runs on a separate device like a tablet While many interpreters rely on third-party ASR tools, these can introduce complexity and raise data privacy concerns. Try Now Table of Contents: Introduction Enable Language Interpretation in Zoom Adding Interpreters to your Meeting or Webinar Initiating Interpretation Sessions Managing Language Interpretation Participant's Experience with Language Interpretation Important Reminders and Considerations Conclusion Enable Language Interpretation in Zoom In today's globally interconnected world, effective communication is essential. Zoom's language interpretation feature can bridge language barriers and allow participants to connect in multiple languages. By enabling this feature, you can provide a seamless and inclusive meeting or webinar experience for all attendees. To enable language interpretation in Zoom, first, sign in to your Zoom web portal at zoom.us. Once logged in, navigate to Settings from the left menu. In the In Meeting (Advanced) section, you'll find the Language Interpretation option. Click the toggle to enable or disable the feature. By default, Zoom offers nine languages for interpretation. However, you can also add custom languages by clicking the plus sign. Keep in mind that the maximum number of custom languages that can be chosen during a meeting is five. If you require more custom languages, reach out to Zoom Support for assistance. Adding Interpreters to your Meeting or Webinar To ensure a smooth interpretation experience, it is important to add qualified interpreters to your meeting or webinar. Scheduling a meeting with automatic generation of the Meeting ID is the first step to add an interpreter. After scheduling the meeting, scroll down to the Interpretation section. Enter the email address of the interpreter and select the appropriate languages for them. Save the meeting to finalize the changes. If you need to make any modifications to the interpreter's details like adding more interpreters, resending email invitations, or removing an interpreter, you can do so by clicking the Edit option under the interpreter's section. Remember to click Save after making any changes. For webinars, the process for adding interpreters is the same as that for meetings. Schedule the webinar and follow the steps Mentioned above to ensure language interpretation is available to participants. Initiating Interpretation Sessions Once you launch your meeting or webinar, you can initiate the interpretation sessions. In the meeting controls, locate the Interpretation option and click on it. From there, you can add additional interpreters if needed. When you are ready to start the interpretation session, click Start. This step will enable interpreters and participants to access the interpretation feature. Interpreters can select the language Channel assigned to them, allowing them to hear the original meeting audio, which they can then Translate. Managing Language Interpretation As the host, you have the ability to manage language interpretation during the meeting or webinar. By clicking on the Interpretation option in the meeting controls, you can end the interpretation session or make changes to the interpreter settings. It is important to note that interpreters can only select the language channel assigned to them. On the other HAND, participants can choose their preferred language channel and hear the translated audio along with the original audio at a lower volume. This allows participants to understand tone and intonation for better comprehension. If participants prefer to only hear the interpreter, they have the option to mute the original audio. Participant's Experience with Language Interpretation To fully utilize the language interpretation feature, participants must join the meeting or webinar via computer audio. Telephone dial-in users do not have access to this feature. Once joined, participants can click on the Interpretation option in the meeting controls and select their desired language channel. By providing participants with the option to choose their language channel, Zoom ensures inclusivity and enhances the meeting experience for individuals who require interpretation services. Participants can seamlessly communicate and understand the content being shared, fostering effective collaboration. Important Reminders and Considerations While using the language interpretation feature, there are a few important reminders to keep in mind. Language interpretation cannot be used in meetings using Personal Meeting ID (PMI) or Instant Meetings. It is only available in scheduled meetings where the Generate Automatically option is selected for the Meeting ID. To ensure optimal audio quality during interpretation sessions, it is recommended to avoid sharing computer audio simultaneously. This could cause audio imbalances due to full-volume broadcasting. Conclusion With Zoom's language interpretation feature, breaking down language barriers in meetings and webinars has become easier than ever before. By following the steps outlined in this guide, you can enable language interpretation, add interpreters, and provide a seamless multilingual experience for all participants. Participants can choose their preferred language channel for seamless communication. Join via computer audio for full participation in interpretation sessions. Language interpretation is not available for meetings using Personal Meeting ID or Instant Meetings. FAQ: Q: Can custom languages be added after a meeting or webinar has been scheduled? A: No, custom languages can only be added during the scheduling process. If you require additional custom languages, you can contact Zoom Support for assistance. Q: How many interpreters can be added to a meeting or webinar? A: There is no set limit to the number of interpreters that can be added. You can add as many interpreters as you need to ensure effective interpretation services. Q: Is language interpretation available for telephone dial-in users? A: No, language interpretation is only accessible for participants who join via computer audio. Telephone dial-in users do not have access to this feature. Q: Can participants hear both the translated audio and the original audio during interpretation sessions? A: Yes, participants have the option to hear both the translated audio and the original audio at a lower volume. This allows for better understanding of tone and intonation. However, participants can also choose to mute the original audio and only hear the interpreter. Available on Android and iOS in February, the app brings both AI and human-powered speech translation and captions to any smartphone or tablet. Its new and unique “meet now” feature also allows users to share a session on other devices to have their conversations translated back-and-forth continuously and instantly. Designed for on-demand language accessibility, KUDO Mobile App v.2.0 offers two options: to join an existing session (meeting or event) using human interpretation or AI speech translation, or to create an instant live session using AI-translated audio and captions only from the app itself. Users can participate in both in-person and virtual conversations in 200+ spoken or sign languages (human interpretation) or 50+ languages (KUDO AI) by speaking, listening, and reading captions in the language of their choice — all within a highly customizable interface. Additionally, all the features of the KUDO Platform are available within the mobile app, such as voting and polling, file-sharing, request-to-speak, a virtual lobby, and more. Where KUDO Mobile App v.2.0 differs from the likes of Chat-GPT and Google Translate is in its real-time, continuous approach to speech translation; rather than a record-and-playback tool that deals with translations sentence-by-sentence, users can expect continuous translation throughout their entire conversations. After signing into their KUDO account and clicking “meet now,” users can set the language(s) they need, then share the session code with others who can immediately join the conversation from their own devices. This makes it perfectly adapted to holding in-person communication in the language of everyone’s choice, bridging the gap between the purely corporate world and newer, consumer-facing use cases for AI speech translation. “Our revamped mobile app sets a new standard for on-the-go multilingual communication, bringing us a step closer to holding in-person conversations in any language, anywhere,” says Fardad Zabetian, CEO of KUDO. “Whether you’re in a business meeting, sitting in a classroom, performing employee onboarding or training sessions in physical workplaces like factory floors, or attending a worship session, this app ensures that language barriers no longer stand in the way of meaningful dialogue.” Key Features: Native App for Mobile and Tablets: Available on Android and iOS, the app is optimized for both mobile and tablet devices, ensuring a smooth and intuitive user experience. KUDO AI ‘Meet Now’: Users can instantly host multilingual meetings by logging into their account, selecting their desired language(s), and sharing a session code. Participants can join immediately for real-time conversational speech translation. Comprehensive Accessibility: The app offers a fully customizable captioning system, following industry best practices for accessibility. Users can personalize fonts, colors, and sizes to suit their needs. Human and AI Language Support: Speak in any language and receive both audio and text translations in your preferred language(s), powered by either human interpretation or KUDO AI. Multimodal Language Support: Speak in any language and receive both audio and text translations in your preferred language(s). The app’s dual functionality bridges the gap between spoken and visual communication. Legacy Features Maintained: In addition to new capabilities, the app retains all the popular features from the original KUDO Platform, including voting tools, a Q&A functionality, and request-to-speak. Availability: The KUDO mobile app will be available for download on the Apple App Store and Google Play Store in February. Please note that you need to have a KUDO account to use either version of the mobile app. MultiLingual StaffMultiLingual creates go-to news and resources for language industry professionals. content: Knowledge Base Getting Started How to capture a virtual event for KUDO AI Translation Follow the steps below to capture virtual content on a desktop computer and send it to a KUDO meeting for AI translation. In this guide we’ll use a Zoom meeting as the example source, but the same workflow applies when capturing other platforms such as ON24 sessions, pre-recorded videos, and additional virtual sources. AUDIO Please install VB-Cable Join the Zoom meeting as an attendee and mute your microphone and turn off your camera. 2. Set the Speaker (headphone) device to VB-Audio (Virtual Cable)3. Go to Windows' Sound Settings.4. Select 'VB Virtual Cable' as the Output device. This ensures that your computer's desktop audio is sent to the virtual cable.5. Copy the KUDO Meeting's Participant/Speaker Link.6. Open the link on Chrome, enter a Display Name (it will show in recordings), and Email address then click JOIN. If you don't see this page, please log out of your KUDO Client account then rejoin the link.7. If it's your first time using KUDO, click to Allow Chrome to use microphone devices.8. In KUDO Media Settings, select Virtual Audio Cable for Microphone.9. Click to Join the KUDO Meeting.10. Select the source language (floor) audio. 11. Select AI voice speech preference (this will be in the recording). Then click OK. 12. In KUDO, turn ON the Microphone to receive the audio from virtual cable (host platform). Open the AI captions to verify that the AI is receiving the audio. We reccommend muting the 'Audio' (loudspeaker icon) to prevent a feedback loop. VIDEO (optional for AI translation) 13. Please install OBS Join the Zoom meeting as a participant, mute your microphone, turn off your camera, and leave the Zoom window open. 14. Go to the OBS software, go to Sources and click '+' to add a video source.15. Click "Display Capture" to capture your entire desktop display. You may also choose 'Window Capture' to specify capturing the Zoom program window, or 'Media Source' to play a recorded video.16. Click "OK"17. Click the Display Monitor that you wish you capture.18. Click "OK"19. Click "Start Virtual Camera"20. Go to the KUDO Participant/Speaker link to Join the meeting.21. Enter a name (it will show in the recording/stream) and email address then click Join.22. Select OBS Virtual Camera as your camera device.23. Select your microphone and speaker devices then click Join.24. Turn ON your Camera to start receiving video from OBS. OB: Scheduling a KUDO Meeting with AI Translation Set up your first AI-powered meeting, explore key AI settings, and make sure you know exactly where to find the tools you’ll use most. By the end of this guide, you’ll have a fully configured KUDO meeting ready to host participants in multiple languages, with AI handling the translation and captions.Topics: Scheduling a meeting with AI translation (Step 4) Selecting the meeting type and AI modality (Step 7) Adding AI languages to the meeting (Step 9) Finding features, like Recordings, in the meeting dashboard (Step 16) Customizing the AI translator (Step 20) Finding the meeting links, QR code and widget (Step 24) Editing the languages during a live meeting (Step 29 Accessing the post-meeting report (Step 34) And when you're ready, follow these steps to join the meeting. 1. Let’s start by heading to live.kudoway.com to sign in with your KUDO account credentials2. Once you’re logged in, you’ll land on your dashboard. From here, click on the Client role. This is your control center for scheduling meetings, accessing links, and downloading transcriptions3. To schedule a meeting, click New Session and choose AI Speech TranslationScheduling the Meeting4. Give your meeting a clear name so participants know exactly what it’s about5. Next, set the date and start and end time6. By default, your meeting will remain open for an hour after its scheduled end. If you’d prefer it to end exactly on time, enable Force Close Meeting. Please keep in mind that the meeting cannot be re-activated after the meeting ends.AI Meeting types (Modalities) 7. Now, decide how your AI will assist during the meeting: AI Speech and Captions is ideal for presentations, keynotes, and town halls. This includes AI speech translation, captions, multilingual recording, transcription, and customization. 8. AI Captions Only is best for multilingual discussions. Latency is reduced and AI captions are available, but AI speech translation, recording, and the glossary and do-not-translate list are turned off.Adding languages to the Meeting 9. Let's assume that this meeting requires English, Japanese and Korean. The meeting will be held in English, except for one presenter in Japanese. Click Speaker language to add English 10. Click Translation language to add Japanese11. Remember, one presenter will speak in Japanese. Click Speaker Language to add Japanese 12. Finally, click Translation language to add Korean. In this specific language combination: Only English and Japanese will be detected as spoken (source) languages English, Japanese and Korean translation will be available for all attendees Please keep in mind that once the meeting begins, Speaker languages cannot be modified 13. Enter the meeting host’s email address. Meeting hosts can manage participants, record sessions, and end meetings directly from the call14. If you enable Automatic Recording, it will begin as soon as the first participant joins15. When you’re done, click Save to create your meetingNavigating the Meeting dashboard16. Click Users to add meeting a meeting host, or see the overal list of participants17. Click Content to setup a poll or vote, upload files to share with participants, and access the meeting's recordings and transcripts.18. Click Settings to access Meeting Features like the Lobby and the Broadcast suite to configure RTMP and HLS streaming.19. Click AI Customization to leverage KUDO's advanced linguistic featuresAI Customization20. If you have acronyms, product names, or other terms you don’t want translated, go to Do Not Translate21. Add your terms to the Do-Not-Translate list and choose whether they apply to just this meeting or all future ones22. If you have acronyms, technical terms, or other terms you want the AI to recognize, go to AI Customization then Word Priority23. Add your terms to the Word Priority list and choose whether they apply to just this meeting or all future onesMeeting links, QR codes and widgets 24. KUDO offers several ways for people to join. The Participant and Speaker Link gives full camera and microphone access in their preferred language. This link is also used for upstreaming on-site audio for events, joining "Meet Now" meetings on the app, and integrating with Microsoft Teams meetings. 25. The Viewer-Only Link is for browser-based livestream viewing with AI translation. Users enter an email address to join the livestream on the KUDO Meeting platform without access to camera, microphone, or chat.26. The KUDO Widget embeds the AI translation into websites or event platforms27. The KUDO Mobile Link is a quick browser or QR code access to AI speech and captions28. Click Play to manually start the meeting and allow participants to access KUDOChanging the Meeting's languages29. Let's assume that we need to add Russian while the meeting is live. Click Edit Meeting to access the language settings.30. Because the meeting is live, Russian can only be added as a Translation, or target, language31. Click Update to request the language32. Lastly, click Restart for the change to take place. Users will need to refresh KUDO to see the new language in the language selector33. Click Stop to end the meeting, streaming, and access to the platform. The meeting cannot be restarted after it has ended34. After the meeting, you can find the post-meeting report in Meeting Statistics How to join a KUDO AI Meeting as a Participant This guide explains how to join a KUDO Meeting using the Participant/Speaker link whether you're presenting in KUDO, or capturing a virtual or in-person meeting.Navigate to the Participant/Speaker link provided by the host.Use Chrome, Firefox or Edge browsersWear a headset for the best experienceEnter your email address, then click Join.Select your preferred camera device (optional).Select your preferred microphone and speaker device, then click Join.Choose the spoken (source) language, then click OK.Click the microphone icon to unmute and begin speaking or streaming audio.Enable Closed Captions to confirm that AI is receiving the source speech.IMPORTANT: If the spoken language changes, update the source language selection in "You are speaking". How to Stream Your KUDO AI Meeting to YouTube in Multiple Languages Streaming your KUDO AI meeting to YouTube allows your audience to follow along in their preferred language with AI speech translation. In this guide we'll create two YouTube livestreams, one for English and one for Spanish, and connect them to KUDO using its RTMP Broadcast feature. Follow the interactive walkthrough: Open Tutorial Setting up YouTube Streams Open YouTube Studio and click Schedule Stream. Name your stream clearly and include the language (e.g., “Multilingual Livestream – English”). Choose your preferred start method: Auto-start ON > YouTube goes live automatically when KUDO begins broadcasting. Auto-start OFF > You control when the stream starts. Under Stream Key Settings, create a new Stream Key and label it English. This lets you stay orgranized and reuse it in the future. Repeat the process to schedule a Spanish stream: create another scheduled stream, assign a new Spanish stream key, and save it for later use. You can continue adding more streams for additional languages, as long as each has a unique key. Connecting YouTube Streams to KUDO Open your KUDO Meeting Dashboard. Go to Settings > Broadcast and toggle Broadcast ON. Click Add RTMP Stream and configure your English livestream: Select YouTube Live as the Casting Medium. Paste the Server URL (this is the same for all YouTube streams). Insert the English stream key. Choose English as the channel. Click Save. Repeat for Spanish: Click Add RTMP Stream again. Select YouTube Live. Paste the same Server URL. Insert the Spanish stream key. Choose Spanish as the channel. Click Save. Going LiveOnce your KUDO meeting is live, return to Broadcast settings and click Start Broadcast.To end streaming, click Stop Broadcast. (Your KUDO meeting continues running even if you stop the livestream, and you can restart anytime.) Routing the KUDO languages to audio distribution systems (Using Dante) KUDO offers two ways to route multilingual audio to external sound systems like FM or IR distribution systems: Method 1: KUDO Audio Manager (this article) – Route all language channels from a single KUDO PC to a Dante network using Dante Virtual Soundcard. This article is an overview. For step-by-step guidance, please contact KUDO support. Method 2: KUDO Mobile Link – Use individual laptops per language with analog outputs. Learn more about Method 2 → When to Use This SetupThis method is ideal for hybrid or in-room meetings that require professional-grade audio distribution via Dante. It supports: Centralized audio routing from a single PC Cleaner, digital audio integration Simultaneous interpretation distribution to multiple channels Seamless hand-off to FM or IR transmitters from Dante outputs Requirements KUDO Meeting with 'Audio Manager' turned ON before the start of the meeting 1 KUDO Audio Manager in the meeting (Chrome browser) 1 PC (Windows preferred) with Dante Virtual Soundcard (DVS) installed and licensed Stable wired internet connection Chrome browser with access to KUDO Access to Dante Controller software (for routing) Dante-enabled audio network (e.g., Yamaha TiO1608-D2, Q-SYS, etc.) Setup Overview1. Prepare the PC Install and activate Dante Virtual Soundcard (DVS) on the PC. Open Dante Controller and confirm the PC is visible on the Dante network. 2. Log In to KUDO Audio Manager Open Google Chrome and go to https://live.kudoway.com Sign in with your KUDO Audio Manager credentials. Navigate to the meeting you'd like to manage. Launch Venue Audio Out from the options. 3. Configure 'Venue Audio Out' In Audio Manager, select Dante Virtual Soundcard as your audio output device. Assign each language channel to a separate Dante output using odd numbers (e.g., Channel 1 = English, Channel 3 = Spanish, Channel 5 = French, etc.) Ensure all interpreter audio channels are receiving signal within KUDO. Each Audio Manager can manage up 8 channels (languages) 4. Route Audio on Dante Controller Open Dante Controller on the same or another PC. Route the output channels from the DVS-equipped PC to the corresponding Dante-enabled hardware (e.g., Yamaha TiO1608-D2 or other DSP/mixer/transmitter input). Verify signal is being received at the endpoint devices. 5. Final Checks Test all language channels prior to the event. Monitor signal levels on Dante Controller and/or DSP interface. Ensure any connected FM or IR systems are receiving clean signals. Tips for Best Results Please use Windows operating systems for optimal integration Always use wired Ethernet for Dante and KUDO PC Disable sleep and power-saving settings on the PC Label each output clearly in Dante Controller Keep backup licenses or a second PC ready if possible Use professional-grade Dante-compatible interfaces or DSPs for optimal integration For macOS Users:When installing Dante Virtual Soundcard (DVS) on macOS, the system only exposes one audio device labeled Dante Virtual Soundcard. To access and route multiple Dante channels, additional software such as Loopback is required. While this setup is more involved and requires a stronger understanding of audio routing, it allows macOS users to fully leverage up to 16 Dante channels. Loopback Setup InstructionsThis configuration enables full multi-channel Dante audio routing on macOS. Create a new virtual device in Loopback. Leave the Source and Output Channels set to their default values. Under Monitors, click the “+” icon and select Dante Virtual Soundcard. Map the Loopback virtual device to the desired Dante channel. Duplicate channels 1, 2, 3, 4, etc., to create as many channels as needed. If you need help configuring your Dante network, contact KUDO support. Routing the KUDO languages to audio distribution systems (Using KUDO Mobile Link) KUDO offers two primary methods for routing interpretation audio to external sound systems like FM transmitters or infrared (IR) audio distribution systems: Option 1: KUDO Audio Manager — Use a single PC to route multiple language channels directly to Dante-enabled systems. Click here to learn more → Option 2: KUDO Mobile Link Method (this article) — Use individual laptops per language to route audio via headphone out or audio interfaces. When to Use This SetupThe KUDO Mobile Link allows attendees to listen to live interpretation via their smartphones. However, routing audio to external receivers can be beneficial when: Smartphones run low on battery or overheat Internet connectivity is unreliable You need a backup/compliance solution using traditional receivers (FM or IR) Equipment Needed 1 laptop per language (Windows/macOS) Wired internet connection for each laptop Google Chrome browser (recommended) Optional: USB audio interface for better quality 3.5mm to RCA/XLR adapters or cables FM transmitter or IR audio distribution system Optional: Ground loop isolators to reduce hum/noise, and adapters. Step-by-Step Setup Guide1. Laptop & Mobile Link Setup Plug in each laptop and connect to reliable internet (Wi-Fi or Ethernet). Open Chrome and navigate to the KUDO Mobile Link for your event. Join the session as a listener on each laptop, selecting one language per device.Example: Laptop 1: Spanish Laptop 2: English Confirm that audio is playing through each laptop using headphones or built-in speakers. 2. Route Audio to the External SystemOption A: Using Headphone Out (Simple) Connect a 3.5mm cable from the laptop headphone jack to your FM or IR transmitter input. Adjust laptop volume to around 70% to avoid distortion. Use a ground loop isolator if you hear hum or interference. Option B: Using USB Audio Interface (Recommended) Connect a USB audio interface to the laptop. Set your system/browser audio to output via the interface. Use the interface’s RCA, 1/4", or XLR outputs to feed your transmitter. This method offers cleaner, more stable audio quality with less chance of interference. 3. Transmit to Attendee Receivers FM Setup: Connect each audio feed to a dedicated FM transmitter. IR Setup: Connect each audio feed to an IR emitter panel. Ensure attendees are tuned into the correct channels/frequencies. Tips for Best Results Clearly label each laptop by language. Use wired internet when available for maximum stability. Disable sleep mode, screen savers, and system notifications on all laptops. Conduct full audio testing before the event. Monitor output during the session. Provide extra FM or IR receivers as backups for attendees. If you need further support with this configuration, contact the KUDO support team. See all 15 articles

page_title: Otter wants to be your AI assistant
meta_description: The company known for transcription software is adding new features to rival Google and Microsoft.
content: Skip to main contentFeb 13, 2024 - TechnologyOtter releases new features for its AI meeting assistantIna Friedfacebook (opens in new window)twitter (opens in new window)linkedin (opens in new window)email (opens in new window)sms (opens in new window)Add Axios on GoogleAdd Axios as your preferred source tosee more of our stories on Google.Add Axios on GoogleA screenshot of a new feature in Otter that allows the AI engine to search across meetings. Image: OtterTranscription software company Otter announced a significant boost to its AI features on Tuesday, including the ability for its AI bot to join text-based chats and to use the technology to search across one's entire meeting history.Why it matters: Otter wants to shift its app from a tool people use to get meeting transcripts to one workers turn to for a wide range of information.Details: In the first of the new features, Otter's AI chatbot, which has been able to answer a wide range of natural-language queries about a specific meeting, will now be able to answer questions based on all of a user's meeting transcripts.Otter offers channels and direct messages for co-workers to collaborate. Now its chatbot will also be able to participate in those text-based channels.There's also an AI-generated conversation summary that works in real-time during a meeting to identify and track action items, including who is delegated to a task and what the deadline is.All three features are included in the company's existing free and paid subscription products. The ability to search across meetings and the AI summaries are available now, while the AI chat in channels feature is starting to roll out for some users and will roll out to others in the coming weeks.Between the lines: Otter is positioning itself as both more affordable than its rivals — since it isn't charging extra for AI features — and more powerful than the capabilities being added to programs like Zoom, Microsoft Teams and Google Meet. Plus, it works across meetings that take place in any of those apps.Yes, but: Microsoft and Google's AI assistants also work in areas where Otter doesn't have products, including email and productivity apps.What's next: Otter is working on allowing chatbots to contribute to live meetings potentially later this year, CEO Sam Liang told Axios. Eventually, Liang sees a world in which each person will have their own chatbot that can pipe in insights and perspective based on its knowledge of how the person has interacted in the past.And while right now Otter only searches data in meetings, Liang said the company is working on how to bring in information from Slack, email and other sources.facebook (opens in new window)twitter (opens in new window)linkedin (opens in new window)email (opens in new window)sms (opens in new window)Add Axios on GoogleWhat to read nextTechnologyFeb 6, 2025AI bots enter the group chatGo deeper (2 min. read)TechnologyFeb 14, 2024Slack taps AI to summarize your long-winded co-workersGo deeper (2 min. read)TechnologyMay 14, 2024ChatGPT's new voice welcomes interruptionsGo deeper (2 min. read)
