Personnalisez vos préférences pour contrôler la manière dont vos informations sont manipulées.Traduction de site webLes meilleurs logiciels de traduction automatique à essayer en 2025Écrit parMerve AlsanRelu parMis à jour le19 décembre 202519 décembre 2025Les entreprises disposent désormais d'une alternative viable aux traducteurs humains pour traduire leurs textes : les logiciels de traduction automatique.Un logiciel de traduction automatique (ou logiciel MT, pour Machine Translation) s'appuie sur l'intelligence artificielle pour traduire instantanément des textes d'une langue à l'autre, par exemple de l'anglais vers le français et vice-versa. Si les traducteurs automatiques n'offraient pas une grande précision de traduction lorsqu'ils ont initialement été développés, les progrès technologiques effectués au cours des dernières décennies permettent désormais à ces outils de fournir des résultats d'une précision satisfaisante.Ces logiciels sont donc souvent intégrés aux outils de traduction assistée par ordinateur (TAO) et utilisés par les entreprises qui développent des projets à l'échelle mondiale. Par exemple, les entreprises internationales qui souhaitent localiser leurs pages web peuvent faire appel à un outil de traduction automatique pour traduire d'importants volumes de texte.Mais les logiciels de traduction automatique ne servent pas uniquement à traduire des sites web. Ils peuvent également fournir une première traduction pour des textes techniques, des textes juridiques ou tous autres documents nécessaires à l'entretien de bonnes relations d'affaires entre entités internationales. D'un point de vue financier, investir dans la traduction présente des avantages évidents : selon une étude réalisée par Common Sense Advisory (aujourd'hui connu sous le nom de CSA Research), les entreprises du classement Fortune 500 qui dépensent davantage en traduction ont 1,5 fois plus de chances que leurs homologues de voir leur chiffre d'affaires global augmenter.Avec l’évolution rapide de ces technologies, de nombreuses entreprises se demandent aujourd'hui quel est le meilleur logiciel de traduction automatique pour un usage professionnel, quels logiciels offrent la meilleure précision linguistique, quels logiciels possèdent des fonctionnalités de traduction en temps réel ou proposent un essai gratuit. Dans cet article, nous allons explorer les principaux logiciels de traduction automatique, comparer leurs points forts et leurs limites et vous montrer comment mettre en œuvre un processus efficace pour la traduction des pages web de votre entreprise.Remarque : vous cherchez un outil pour traduire votre site web ? Profitez des 14 jours d'essai gratuit de Weglot et découvrez comment tirer parti de la traduction IA pour lancer instantanément un site web multilingue. Les avantages des logiciels de traduction de sites webSi certaines des plus grandes entreprises du marché placent la traduction au rang de leurs priorités et font appel à des logiciels spécialisés, c'est avant tout parce que c'est rentable.Les personnes dont l'anglais est la langue maternelle représentent moins de 5 % de la population mondiale, alors que 52 % des sites web sont rédigés en anglais. Beaucoup d'entreprises se privent donc de marchés sur lesquels elles pourraient s'épanouir. En effet, alors que les contenus publiés sur Internet s'adressent en majorité aux anglophones, les consommateurs sont 73 % plus enclins à acheter sur un site web disponible dans leur langue maternelle. Les grandes entreprises en sont conscientes. Microsoft, par exemple, a traduit ses produits dans plus de 90 langues, Toshiba dans plus de 30 et Apple dans 40.À long terme, la traduction de votre site web boostera vos ventes et renforcera votre travail de marketing, notamment en matière de référencement naturel. Plus de la moitié des recherches effectuées sur Google ne sont pas en langue anglaise. Comment devancer alors vos concurrents internationaux si vous ne créez pas de contenu dans la langue maternelle de votre public cible ? La réponse est simple : mission impossible. C'est là que les logiciels de traduction automatique entrent en jeu. La traduction automatique peut vous aider à localiser votre site web et à améliorer votre SEO multilingue afin d'élargir votre marché. De fait, les visiteurs non anglophones s'intéresseront plus facilement à votre site web s'ils lisent des contenus dans leur langue maternelle. Pour plus de 56 % des consommateurs, obtenir des informations dans leur langue est plus important que le prix. Aujourd'hui, la plupart des navigateurs intègrent des fonctionnalités permettant d'utiliser des traducteurs en ligne classiques (via des systèmes de traduction automatique avancés). Cependant, beaucoup de locuteurs natifs préfèrent qu'un site web leur soit proposé dès le départ dans leur langue, car cela leur évite de traduire manuellement les textes à l'aide de leurs applications de traduction habituelles.Prenons l'exemple de respond.io. Cette plateforme de gestion de la relation clients a utilisé Weglot pour traduire son site web dans quinze nouvelles langues. Depuis l'intégration de la solution, le site a multiplié par deux son trafic et ses impressions. Si respond.io a atteint ces résultats, il n'y a pas de raison que vous ne puissiez pas bénéficier de performances similaires !L'évolution de la traduction automatique jusqu'en 2025 (et au-delà) Soyons honnêtes : à ses origines, la traduction automatique n'était pas optimale.Années 1950 : création du premier système de traduction automatique. Années 1970 : début du développement des technologies de reconnaissance vocale. Années 1980 : arrivée des dictionnaires électroniques et des bases de données terminologiques.Années 1990 : introduction de la traduction automatique statistique et des outils de traduction assistée par ordinateur (TAO).2006 : lancement de Google Traduction.2016 : intégration de la traduction automatique neuronale dans Google Traduction.Les premières expériences de traduction automatique remontent aux années 1950, avec les systèmes précurseurs utilisant la traduction automatique basée sur des règles (RBMT). La technologie RBMT s'est ensuite développée jusqu'à mobiliser, dans les années 1970, un ensemble de règles grammaticales et de dictionnaires bilingues pour traduire les textes. Cependant, ces systèmes produisaient souvent des traductions littérales et rigides, car ils avaient du mal à appréhender les nuances linguistiques.La traduction automatique s'est ainsi forgé dès ses débuts une mauvaise réputation. Peu impressionnés par la faible précision des textes issus des outils de traduction automatique, les gens ont commencé à les rejeter au motif qu'ils étaient de moins bonne qualité que le travail réalisé par les traducteurs humains, et ont privilégié les services de traduction de sites web pour localiser leurs contenus.De la traduction automatique basée sur des règles à la traduction automatique statistiqueHeureusement pour les fournisseurs de traduction automatique, elle a commencé à se défaire de cette image négative avec les progrès de la technologie. Après la RBMT est venue la traduction automatique statistique (SMT pour statistical machine translation), qui traduit un texte en analysant un corpus de textes bilingues (à savoir des traductions humaines existantes). Elle utilise ensuite des algorithmes prédictifs pour déterminer la meilleure façon de traduire un texte dans un contexte donné.Si la SMT représentait une amélioration majeure par rapport à la RBMT, sa précision laissait encore parfois à désirer. Mais les progrès ne se sont pas arrêtés là. Aujourd'hui, la dernière – et la meilleure – technologie de traduction automatique disponible est la traduction automatique neuronale (NMT, neural machine translation), qui utilise des modèles complexes d'apprentissage profond pour traduire les textes.L'avènement de la traduction automatique neuronaleLa traduction automatique neuronale est capable de générer des résultats de haute qualité grâce à des algorithmes de traduction linguistique sophistiqués. Ces traductions sont non seulement plus précises, mais elles semblent également plus naturelles que les traductions produites par les technologies RMBT et SMT.Aujourd'hui, l'efficacité de la NMT a eu raison des principales oppositions à la traduction automatique. Même les objections du type « La traduction automatique ne peut pas détecter ou traduire les textes contenus dans des images et des diapositives PowerPoint » ont été vaincues : les outils de traduction automatique avancés peuvent désormais le faire.L'IA générative : l'avenir des logiciels de traduction automatique ? L'essor des grands modèles de langage (LLM) et de l'IA générative en 2022-2023 a ouvert de nouvelles perspectives pour la traduction automatique. Contrairement aux systèmes de traduction neuronale traditionnels, qui sont spécifiquement conçus pour traduire des textes entre différentes paires de langues, les modèles d'IA générative sont entraînés sur d'importants volumes de données multilingues et peuvent ainsi faire preuve d'une compréhension plus globale du contexte selon les langues.Ces modèles d'IA promettent de mieux gérer les nuances linguistiques, notamment les expressions idiomatiques, les références culturelles et les interprétations dépendantes du contexte, qui ont toujours constitué un défi pour la traduction automatique. Par exemple, ils parviennent souvent à maintenir un ton et un style cohérents sur de longs textes, et certains sont même capables d'adapter les traductions à des secteurs ou à des publics spécifiques.Cependant, il est important de savoir que l'IA générative ne remplace pas totalement la NMT. Au contraire, de nombreux prestataires de services de traduction explorent des approches hybrides qui allient les points forts des deux technologies. Cela permettrait de combiner la fiabilité et l'efficacité de la NMT traditionnelle avec la compréhension du contexte et l'adaptabilité de l'IA générative.Devez-vous utiliser un logiciel de traduction automatique pour votre entreprise ? Choisir le meilleur logiciel de traduction automatique pour un usage professionnel dépend de plusieurs critères : précision linguistique, intégrations, options de personnalisation, support multilingue avancé. Aujourd'hui très répandue, la traduction automatique constitue une véritable bouée de sauvetage pour les entreprises internationales qui ont besoin d'obtenir des traductions cohérentes et précises avec la plus grande efficacité possible. Même les traducteurs professionnels adoptent cette technologie pour rationaliser et accélérer le processus de traduction !Pourquoi donc ? Voici quelques-uns des avantages des logiciels de traduction automatique, dont votre entreprise pourrait également profiter :Facilité d'utilisation : les logiciels de traduction automatique sont si simples à appliquer qu'il n'est pas nécessaire d'avoir des connaissances techniques pour les utiliser comme les pros. Lancez le logiciel, copiez-collez votre texte source, définissez votre langue cible et obtenez la traduction en temps réel de votre texte.Rapidité : les logiciels de traduction automatique sont capables de traduire un texte en quelques secondes, alors qu'une traduction humaine peut demander plusieurs heures, voire plusieurs jours, en fonction du volume de texte. Fiabilité : si la précision des traductions réalisées à l'aide de traducteurs automatiques reste variable, le résultat est globalement fiable. En règle générale, ces logiciels sont contrôlés par des traducteurs experts et des locuteurs natifs avant d'être lancés.Excellent rapport qualité-prix : il est beaucoup moins coûteux d'investir dans un logiciel de traduction automatique que de faire appel à un traducteur professionnel, surtout si vous souhaitez traduire des paires de langues peu courantes ou si vous avez besoin de traductions rapides.Fonctionnement fluide : certains logiciels de traduction automatique peuvent s'intégrer à d'autres plateformes pour fluidifier le processus. Adieu les copier-coller fastidieux entre le logiciel et la plateforme !Voici un aperçu de la traduction d'un site web à l'aide de l'IA :6 des meilleurs logiciels de traduction automatique sur le marché Quels logiciels de traduction automatique offrent la meilleure précision linguistique ? À l'heure actuelle, il n'existe pas d'outil de traduction automatique capable de répondre parfaitement à tous les besoins et à tous les cas d'usage. Chaque logiciel a ses avantages et ses inconvénients et peut mieux se prêter à certains objectifs, formats et publics cibles que d'autres.Dans ce comparatif, vous découvrirez 6 des meilleurs logiciels de traduction automatique disponibles sur le marché, ainsi qu'une analyse de l'impact de leurs caractéristiques technologiques sur la qualité des traductions :1. Weglot Avec cet outil de traduction de sites web qui allie la rapidité de la traduction automatique à l'intégration directe sur la plateforme de votre site web, vous ne perdrez plus de temps à copier-coller les textes traduits. Weglot est la solution idéale pour obtenir une première couche de traduction automatique pour vos sites web. Nous utilisons les meilleurs moteurs de traduction automatique (DeepL Translator, Microsoft Translator, Google Traduction) pour traduire votre site web avec une grande précision grâce à des fonctionnalités de post-édition avancées. Contrairement aux simples traducteurs instantanés, Weglot propose une solution complète pour les sites web professionnels avec des traductions en temps réel, un essai gratuit et une gestion SEO multilingue intégrée.Weglot s'intègre à WordPress, Shopify, Webflow et toutes les autres plateformes de sites web courantes (sans oublier les sites web personnalisés) pour traduire le contenu de vos pages et afficher le résultat sur votre site web. Vous bénéficiez ainsi d'une solution complète pour la traduction de vos sites web.L'outil est également conçu pour faciliter la collaboration entre vos équipes et des traducteurs professionnels. Vous pouvez donc solliciter facilement un regard professionnel sur vos traductions avant de les publier.Avantages :S'intègre directement aux plateformes les plus courantes (WordPress, Shopify, Webflow, sites personnalisés)Détecte automatiquement les contenus et affiche la traductionInclut des fonctions de collaboration pour la gestion des traductionsOffre des possibilités de post-édition via le tableau de bord WeglotTraduit l'intégralité du site web, y compris les widgets et les balises méta Propose un sélecteur de langues personnalisableProcessus d'installation facile, en particulier sur WordPressTrès bien noté sur G2 en tant que leader du secteurInconvénients :Essai gratuit limité à une langue et 2 000 motsNécessite une formule payante pour ajouter des langues et traiter un plus grand nombre de motsDemande une clé API pour l'installationLes traductions doivent être révisées pour une qualité optimaleNote des utilisateurs : 4,8/5 étoiles2. Google TraductionGoogle Traduction : le nom vous dit sûrement quelque chose ! Souvent considéré comme le traducteur instantané de référence, il s'agit probablement du logiciel de traduction automatique le plus connu sur le marché. Lancé en 2006 et prenant actuellement en charge 133 langues, cet outil de traduction utilisait auparavant la technologie SMT pour livrer des traductions mot à mot. Depuis, Google a abandonné la SMT au profit de la NMT, plus précise, d'où une amélioration constante de la qualité des traductions. Baptisée Google Neural Machine Translation (GNMT), la technologie de traduction automatique propriétaire de Google utilise des réseaux de neurones récurrents pour traduire des phrases entières en préservant autant que possible leur signification en contexte.Google Traduction proposera bientôt des traductions encore plus contextualisées. Ainsi, si vous cherchez un endroit où garer votre voiture ou si vous souhaitez vous promener dans le parc le plus proche, la plateforme fournira le contexte qui lui permettra d'utiliser les bons mots pour assurer la justesse de la traduction. Au nombre des premières langues à bénéficier de cette fonctionnalité figurent l'anglais, le français, l'allemand, le japonais et l'espagnol.Avantages : Prend en charge un très grand nombre de langues (133)Utilise la technologie avancée de traduction automatique neuronale (GNMT)Gratuit et facile d'accèsIntègre désormais des options de traduction en contexte pour certaines langues clés (anglais, français, allemand, japonais et espagnol)Traduit des phrases entières en tenant compte du contexteInconvénients :Qualité parfois inégale, notamment dans les paires de langues moins courantesGère plus difficilement les contenus techniques ou spécialisésPas de possibilités de personnalisation pour des secteurs ou des terminologies spécifiquesFonctionnalités limitées par rapport aux outils de traduction professionnelsPas d'outils d'assurance qualité intégrésPas optimal pour traduire des documents officiels ou commerciaux sans contrôle humainNote des utilisateurs : 4,5/5 étoiles3. DeepL TraducteurDeepL est un service de traduction automatique conçu par Linguee GmbH (désormais DeepL GmbH), une entreprise allemande spécialisée dans le développement de technologies de traduction automatique grâce à l'apprentissage profond. Lancé en 2017, DeepL propose actuellement 32 langues. Le système étudie de manière approfondie et apprend les meilleures manières de traduire à partir de sources fiables. Grâce à l'utilisation de l'intelligence artificielle, DeepL peut fournir des traductions plus justes et plus nuancées que ses concurrents. Il pourrait bien tenir sa promesse d'être « le traducteur le plus précis du monde ».En janvier 2024, DeepL a ajouté l'arabe, cinquième langue la plus parlée au monde. Actuellement disponible sur le traducteur web et sur les applications de bureau et mobiles, il s'agit de la première langue s'écrivant de droite à gauche prise en charge par la solution. Les entreprises peuvent enfin s'adresser à plus de 400 millions d'arabophones en utilisant le service DeepL.Avantages :Précision de traduction globalement supérieure à celle de concurrents tels que Google Trad.Système d'apprentissage adaptatif qui s'améliore au fil du temps en fonction des données fournies par les utilisateursInterface conviviale, facile à installer et immédiatement utilisable Haut niveau de gratuité adapté aux besoins des utilisateurs individuelsAffichage rapide des traductionsRésultats de qualité professionnelle pour les paires de langues les plus courantesInconvénients :Certains utilisateurs signalent des problèmes de stabilité nécessitant parfois une réinstallation.Les notifications invitant constamment à passer à DeepL Pro peuvent être intrusives pour les utilisateurs de la version gratuite.Restrictions techniques en cas d'association de segments de textePrise en charge d'un nombre limité de langues (32 seulement) par rapport à la concurrenceNécessité de souscrire un abonnement payant pour bénéficier de fonctionnalités avancées et traduire plus de motsToutes les paires de langues ne sont pas disponiblesNote des utilisateurs : 4,8/5 étoiles4. content: Les 5 meilleurs outils de traduction audio en 2025 : comparatif et avis Si vous avez déjà essayé de réutiliser un podcast international ou un extrait audio, vous savez à quel point c'est difficile. Vous téléchargez le fichier dans un outil de traduction en ligne gratuit et vous obtenez des phrases hachées, du contexte manquant et une transcription incomplète.Le meilleur traducteur vocal simplifie la vie des professionnels et des créateurs de contenu. il comprend le contexte, préserve le ton et fournit des traductions audio prêtes à l'emploi dans plusieurs formats. trouvez l'outil de traduction automatique qui vous convient et gagnez du temps.J'ai testé plusieurs options disponibles. D'après mon expérience, voici les meilleurs outils de traduction audio, de transcription et de sous-titrage pour celles qui ne se laissent pas arrêter par les barrières linguistiques. Précision de la transcription et gestion du contexteUn bon traducteur audio pour la transcription Fonctionne en deux étapes : d'abord, il transcrit fidèlement la parole en texte, puis il traduit le sens. Recherchez des outils qui préservent le ton, les expressions idiomatiques et le contexte, et proposent des traductions naturelles plutôt que littérales.2. Prise en charge de la transcription multilinguePlus un outil prend en charge de nombreuses langues et dialectes, plus il est polyvalent: c'est particulièrement utile si vous gérez du contenu mondial, des clients internationaux ou des projets multilingues.3. Rapidité et automatisation des tâchesLe meilleur traducteur vocal doit transcrire et traduire rapidement de gros fichiers audio, détecter automatiquement la langue parlée et automatiser des tâches via API.4. Options d'exportation de fichiersTélécharger des transcripts dans plusieurs formats (TXT, SRT, VTT) et partager des liens privés depuis l'éditeur vous fera gagner beaucoup de temps dans votre flux de travail.5. Sécurité, confidentialité et protection des donnéesSi vous téléversez des enregistrements clients ou des fichiers confidentiels, choisissez un traducteur qui protège vos données. content: 9 most common text-to-speech software (plus functions)Written by Indeed Editorial TeamUpdated 27 November 2025Text to speech (TTS) software is an excellent resource for reading digital information, such as documents aloud from desktops, laptops or other devices. It was originally intended as accessibility software for individuals with low vision or reading difficulties, but as the technology improves, it has helped all types of individuals boost their productivity. With so many iterations of TTS software available, it's important to research what's available to find the right one for your needs. In this article, we outline the best text-to-speech software and include some free-to-use applications too.What is text to speech software?Text to speech software is a form of assistive technology that converts text into audio. It works across a multitude of devices, including desktop computers, tablets and smartphones. Text to speech software uses a computer-generated voice that has an adjustable reading speed and other features, such as word highlighting.Some applications even have optical character recognition that allows the software to describe what an image looks like. We initially used text to speech software as an accessibility program for users with reading difficulties. Thanks to technological improvements in TTS software, it has become a useful tool for general productivity in working environments.Search jobs and companies hiring nowJob title, keywords or companyLocationSearchCommon TTS softwareThere are countless TTS applications available today that provide a wide range of functionality and features. Below is a list of the common software options available today:1. PollyPolly is an intelligent TTS application developed by Amazon that uses artificial intelligence to translate text into speech. It uses deep learning techniques to transform the text into speech and can pick up on mannerisms and colloquialisms. It's particularly useful for software engineers and developers who are looking to implement speech input into their own applications.The API of this program is a powerful way to integrate speech into e-books, articles and large bodies of text. It's an intuitive, easy-to-use application that can store the audio in a variety of formats, such as MP3 or PCM files. It also supports a number of languages and dialects, including English, French, German and Russian. Polly has a pricing structure that measures the amount of text translated, so the more you use it, the pricier it gets.2. Linguatec voice readerLinguatec voice reader is a reputable TTS application developed by Linguatec who has been at the forefront of text to speech solutions for a number of years. It is a robust piece of software that converts text into audio files. The home edition of the software is suitable for converting text from Word documents, emails, articles and PDFs into audio files quickly and effectively. It's a comprehensive application with 67 different voices and support of 45 languages including French, Italian and Spanish.Linguatec voice reader typically helps improve user productivity and makes the work easier. You can automatically translate entire text lectures or presentations into an audio form, which can help identify grammatical errors or improve the uptake of information. It also features an intuitive user interface that lets you adjust the audio pitch, speed and volume.Related: How to mindfully improve your personal development3. Capti personalCapti personal has had great success in the education sector and helps improve reading and speech comprehension. This TTS software helps make it easy to listen to anything written and helps overcome language barriers in the process. It works as an online or offline solution and supports over 20 different languages. It focuses on improving active reading and works across articles, websites and e-books.Capti personal is compatible with a number of cloud solutions such as Microsoft OneDrive or Dropbox, making it easy to access across a wide range of devices. There is a free version available for personal use that comes loaded with functionality. For improved voice samples and additional features, there is also a paid version available.4. NaturalReaderNaturalReader is a cloud-based TTS application that doesn't require any software installation and provides online and software free versions and a commercial fee version. Users can convert text taken from various mediums, such as PDF files, e-books or text documents into speech. As it uses cloud technology, NaturalReader is accessible from a variety of devices that are compatible with online use. You can directly upload documents from cloud storage for translation too, which streamlines the conversion from text to speech.It comes equipped with a lot of functionality, including 56 human-sounding voices across nine languages, including American English, British English, French and German. It also supports a wide variety of file formats from text documents to images. It can even handle ePub files and MP3 audio clips.Related: 6 simple tips for how to work hard and stay motivated5. Voice dream readerVoice dream reader is a TTS application designed for mobile devices. It's a useful application that allows for text to speech conversion from a variety of formats, including documents, web pages and e-books. Voice dream reader emphasises natural-sounding voices, with over 180 different options available. It can also understand over 30 languages, including Arabic, English, French and Japanese.It's an excellent text to speech application for productivity because it focuses on mobile devices. You can listen to web articles while on the go or use one of the distraction-free modes to focus on the audio. Voice dream reader is compatible with a number of other cloud solutions, such as Dropbox and Google Drive to effortlessly send files to your mobile device.6. BalabolkaBalabolka is a versatile, free-to-use TTS application that works in a few different ways. You can copy and paste text directly into Balabolka or you can import files using the supported formats such as PDF, HTML or DOC. There are eight different voices available to choose from on the Microsoft speech platform. Whatever you intend to use Balabolka for, it has a lot of functionality, including pitch and volume adjustment.Balabolka also has a handy tool that allows for the saving of narrations across a wide range of audio file formats, such as MP3 or WAV. If you're converting a long document, you have the ability to create bookmarks so that you can find what you need at-a-glance. In essence, Balabolka offers a comprehensive suite of features considering it's completely free-to-use.Related: A guide to the communication process (verbal and non-verbal)7. NaturalReader online readerNaturalReader online reader is an excellent free-to-use TTS application that works in a few different ways. You can load documents directly into the platform to have them read aloud. It can handle a wide range of file types, including e-book formats and PDF files. It can also translate images of text directly through optical character recognition and read the text aloud.The other way to use NaturealReader online reader is through its floating toolbar. This allows you to highlight bodies of text across any application and translate it into an audio form. This is an excellent option for web browsers, word processors or other third-party applications.8. Panopreter BasicPanopreter Basic is an excellent free-to-use TTS application that focuses on the important features. It works with plain or rich text files, web pages or word processor documents and can translate text into a WAV or MP3 audio format. It's a relatively barebones application, but it has a few useful features, such as options to change the language of the text.Other than that, there is very little additional functionality in Panopreter Basic. If you're in need of something more advanced, such as different voice options, then Panopreter does offer a paid-for service too. Advanced features for the paid version include toolbars for Word, additional voices and the ability to highlight bodies of text.Related: A guide to managing a heavy workload (with advice and tips)9. WordTalkWordTalk is a toolbar extension for Word that adds text to speech functionality to the popular word processor. It's compatible with all the iterations of Word and integrates into the interface via a toolbar or ribbon. WordTalk supports SAPI 4 and SAPI 5 voices, which you can quickly adjust to suit your needs. You can select individual words, sentences or paragraphs that are then read aloud and you can save the narrations for later use. There are even a number of keyboard shortcuts available to help increase productivity while using WordTalk. Overall, it's an excellent free-to-use text to speech application.Related:Please note that none of the companies mentioned in this article are affiliated with Indeed. The information on this site is provided as a courtesy and for informational purposes only. content: VoicyPricingTry for free12 Best Speech to Text for Windows Apps (2025 Review)July 16, 2025Are you a busy professional drafting reports, a student working on a project, or a content creator creating articles? The right speech-to-text tool for Windows can dramatically boost your productivity. Speaking is 3x faster than typing.Finding the right tool can be time-consuming, though.This guide takes care of the research for you. Each tool on this list was tried by us, and we're going to remain as objective as possible when we review them. Short version of the articleThe right tool depends on your use-case. If you want basic + accurate speech-to-text on your Windows laptop, these are our picks: Voicy - Best-in-class accuracy, speed, and price, but no voice-commandsDragon professional - Great accuracy, voice commands, but costs +$600Braina Pro - Great accuracy but unintuitive user interfaceMicrosoft Dictate - Free but inconsistent accuracyIf you want to transcribe large audio files, choose these: Otter.ai - Generous free tier, sometimes performs unreliably with heavy accentsSpeechnotes - Free, limited features, only works in the browserRiverside - High accuracy but not specifically built for transcriptionsIf you are a developer who needs a speech-to-text API: OpenAI Whisper API - Incredible accuracy, low latency, affordableIBM Watson - Less accurate than OpenAI, but model can be highly customizedSpeechmatics - Offers streamed transcriptions, but can be pricy1. VoicyVoicy emerges as a powerful and exceptionally versatile speech to text for Windows solution, establishing itself as a standout choice for users seeking best-in-class accuracy and seamless workflow integration.Whether drafting an email in Outlook, collaborating on a report in Google Docs, or messaging on WhatsApp, Voicy allows you to dictate directly into the text field with a simple keyboard shortcut. This eliminates the need to copy and paste from a separate dictation window, creating a fluid and efficient experience.Key Strengths & FeaturesWhat truly sets Voicy apart is its sophisticated AI engine. It doesn't just convert speech; it understands context. The platform achieves over 99% accuracy while automatically handling punctuation and grammar, significantly reducing the need for manual edits. This makes it an invaluable tool for professionals who need to produce polished documents quickly.Furthermore, Voicy’s advanced AI commands provide a unique level of control. You can dictate a casual thought and then instruct the AI to rephrase it into a formal, professional, or even a custom-toned message. Exceptional Accuracy: Achieves over 99% accuracy with automatic punctuation and grammar correction.Universal Compatibility: Works seamlessly across Windows, Mac, and major browsers on thousands of apps like Word, Gmail, and ChatGPT.AI-Powered Editing: Use voice commands to instantly change the tone and style of your dictated text.Multilingual Support: Highly accurate transcription in more than 50 languages.Pros vs ConsPros:Works with every app and websiteAmazing accuracy (99%+)AI can change your writing style instantlySupports 50+ languagesNo copying and pasting neededCons:Needs internet connection to workPremium tool, so it costs moneyPractical ConsiderationsAs a cloud-based service, it also relies on a stable internet connection for optimal performance. However, for users seeking to dramatically boost productivity, enhance accessibility, or simply reduce typing strain, Voicy provides a robust and intelligent solution.Website: usevoicy.com2. Nuance Communications – Dragon Professional IndividualFor decades, Dragon has been the benchmark in professional-grade dictation, and its latest iteration, Dragon Professional Individual, solidifies its position as a powerhouse speech to text for Windows solution.It stands out by learning your specific voice and vocabulary, achieving up to 99% accuracy right out of the box, which improves over time. This makes it ideal for professionals in specialized fields like law or medicine who rely on industry-specific terminology.Beyond simple dictation, Dragon allows for complete hands-free control of your computer. You can create custom voice commands to open applications, insert boilerplate text, or automate multi-step workflows, dramatically boosting productivity.While the one-time cost is significant compared to subscription-based services, its deep integration with Microsoft Office and other business applications provides a seamless user experience that justifies the investment for power users. However, it does require an initial voice training period for optimal performance.Best For: Professionals, academics, and individuals with accessibility needs requiring maximum accuracy and customization.Key Feature: Deep learning engine that continuously adapts to your voice and environmental acoustics.Pricing: A one-time purchase, typically around $699 for a single license.Website: https://www.nuance.com/dragon.htmlPros vs ConsPros:Industry-leading accuracy (up to 99%)Learns your voice and vocabularyComplete computer control with voiceWorks great with Microsoft OfficeOne-time purchase (no monthly fees)Custom voice commandsCons:Expensive upfront cost ($699)Requires voice training setupWindows-focused (limited Mac support)Learning curve for advanced featuresWhile Dragon sets a high standard, its price can be a barrier. For those exploring other options, you can read our guide on affordable alternatives to Dragon Naturally Speaking.3. Braina ProBraina Pro positions itself as more than just a dictation tool; it's a multi-faceted AI virtual assistant that offers a robust speech to text for Windows engine.What sets Braina apart is its extensive language support, accurately transcribing over 90 languages and understanding voice commands. This makes it a highly versatile option for multilingual users or international teams. It also integrates modern AI models like ChatGPT, allowing users to perform complex tasks like drafting emails or summarizing text with simple voice prompts.While the user interface might feel less modern than some competitors, its functionality is powerful. Users can create custom voice commands for nearly any task and even control their PC remotely via a mobile app, adding a layer of convenience not found in many other solutions.The affordable lifetime license is a significant draw for users looking to avoid recurring subscription fees. However, advanced AI features may require purchasing additional credits for heavy usage.Best For: Multilingual professionals, students, and tech enthusiasts looking for a voice-controlled AI assistant with strong dictation capabilities.Key Feature: AI-powered virtual assistant with dictation and voice command support for over 90 languages.Pricing: A one-time purchase of $79 for a lifetime license for Braina Pro.Website: https://www.brainasoft.com/braina/Pros vs ConsPros:Supports 90+ languagesAI assistant features with ChatGPT integrationOne-time purchase (lifetime license)Remote PC control via mobile appCustom voice commandsAffordable at $79Cons:Interface looks outdatedAdvanced AI features may cost extra creditsLearning curve for full functionalityNot as polished as premium competitorsFor users new to this technology, you can learn more about setting up speech-to-text on your system.4. Otter.aiOtter.ai carves out a unique niche by focusing on transcribing conversations, making it an exceptional speech to text for Windows tool for meetings, interviews, and lectures.It excels at real-time transcription, automatically generating a searchable, shareable text record as the conversation happens. Its standout feature is speaker identification, which intelligently tags different speakers in the transcript, transforming a chaotic discussion into an organized, easy-to-follow document. This makes it invaluable for students and professionals who need to capture and review spoken content accurately.Unlike desktop-centric software, Otter.ai is a cloud-based service that seamlessly integrates with video conferencing tools like Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams. Microsoft DictateFor users already embedded in the Microsoft ecosystem, Microsoft Dictate offers an incredibly convenient and powerful speech to text for Windows tool at no extra cost.Integrated directly into Microsoft 365 applications like Word, Outlook, and PowerPoint, it removes the friction of installing third-party software. However, for quick, accessible, and high-quality dictation within your everyday workflow, it’s an unbeatable native solution.Best For: Microsoft 365 subscribers, students, and professionals needing a quick, integrated dictation solution.Key Feature: Native integration within the Microsoft Office suite (Word, Outlook, PowerPoint, OneNote).Pricing: Free for Microsoft 365 subscribers.Website: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365Microsoft's native tool is a strong contender, but it's just one piece of the puzzle. You can get a broader overview by reading our complete guide on Windows speech to text options.Pros vs ConsPros:Completely free with Microsoft 365Built into Office apps (no extra software)Voice commands for editing and formattingReal-time translation featuresMultiple language supportEasy to useCons:Only works in Microsoft Office appsRequires internet for best performanceLimited to Microsoft ecosystemNot as advanced as dedicated tools6. SpeechnotesSpeechnotes offers a streamlined and highly accessible approach to speech to text for Windows users, operating directly within your browser.Its minimalist interface is designed for immediate, distraction-free dictation, making it perfect for quickly capturing thoughts, drafting emails, or taking notes without the friction of installing software or creating an account. The platform distinguishes itself with a continuous dictation mode that doesn't time out, even during long pauses, allowing you to think and speak at your own pace.It effectively leverages Google’s speech recognition engine, providing high accuracy across numerous languages. While it may lack the deep system integration of desktop applications, its simplicity is its greatest strength.Speechnotes includes useful voice commands for punctuation and formatting (e.g., “period,” “new paragraph”), and a Chrome extension allows you to use its functionality across various websites. The core service is completely free, supported by ads, with an optional premium upgrade to remove them and unlock additional features. It is an excellent choice for users who need a reliable, no-fuss transcription tool on the fly.Best For: Students, writers, and casual users needing a quick, free, and browser-based dictation tool.Key Feature: Continuous non-stop dictation and a clean, minimalist editor that requires no login to use.Pricing: Free to use. An optional one-time premium purchase is available to remove ads and add features.Website: https://speechnotes.co/Pros vs ConsPros:Completely free to useNo software installation neededWorks in any browserNo account requiredContinuous dictation (no timeouts)Chrome extension availableVoice commands for punctuationCons:Limited integration with other appsAds in free versionRequires internet connectionBasic features compared to desktop appsNo advanced editing capabilities7. Riverside.fmWhile many tools focus on real-time dictation, Riverside.fm carves out a niche for content creators, particularly podcasters and video producers, who need exceptionally accurate post-production transcripts.It’s primarily a high-fidelity remote recording studio that captures local, uncompressed audio and video for each participant. This focus on quality source material is key to its outstanding transcription accuracy, making it a premier speech to text for Windows tool for media professionals who need reliable text for subtitles, show notes, or content repurposing.After recording, Riverside automatically generates a transcript with impressive speed and speaker detection in over 100 languages. Its standout feature is text-based video and audio editing, where deleting text from the transcript also cuts the corresponding media clip, drastically streamlining the editing workflow.While it's not designed for live dictation like composing emails, its precision in converting recorded conversations into text is second to none for its target audience. Access to its full transcription capabilities requires a subscription.Best For: Podcasters, video creators, journalists, and marketers who require high-quality transcripts from recorded interviews or meetings.Key Feature: Text-based media editing that allows you to edit video and audio by simply editing the text in the transcript.Pricing: Free plan with limited transcription. Paid plans start at $15/month (billed annually).Website: https://riverside.fm/Pros vs ConsPros:Exceptional transcription accuracyText-based video/audio editingSpeaker detection in 100+ languagesHigh-quality recording capabilitiesGreat for content creatorsFree plan availableCons:Not for live dictationRequires subscription for full featuresFocused on content creation onlyMore complex than simple dictation toolsBest for recorded content, not real-time8. This platform excels at handling real-time transcription for applications like call center analytics or live captioning and supports batch processing for large audio archives.The key differentiator for this speech to text for Windows backend is its deep customization. Users can train Watson with custom language and acoustic models to recognize specific jargon, product names, or accents, achieving high accuracy in specialized environments.While its setup requires technical expertise and its usage-based pricing can be complex, its scalability and integration with the broader IBM Cloud ecosystem are unparalleled for developers building custom voice-enabled software.Best For: Developers, enterprises, and businesses building custom applications requiring scalable and accurate transcription.Key Feature: Advanced customization through acoustic and language model training for domain-specific terminology.Pricing: A "Lite" free tier is available for testing. Start Your Journey with Motoshare Post Views: 5 Introduction In our increasingly digital and fast-paced world, the ability to convert spoken words into written text has transformed from a niche luxury into a critical business necessity. Speech-to-Text (Transcription) Platforms are software solutions that leverage Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) technology, and sometimes human expertise, to transcribe audio and video recordings into searchable, editable text. These platforms act as a bridge between the fluid nature of conversation and the structured world of documentation, allowing information to be archived, analyzed, and repurposed with ease. The importance of these tools lies in their ability to save thousands of hours of manual labor. Instead of transcribing a one-hour interview by hand—a task that typically takes four to five hours—AI-powered platforms can deliver a draft in minutes. Key real-world use cases include recording corporate meetings for automated minutes, transcribing journalistic interviews, generating captions for social media videos to improve accessibility, and documenting medical or legal consultations where precision is paramount. When choosing a platform, users must evaluate criteria such as accuracy rates (especially with accents or background noise), turnaround time, language support, and the robustness of the built-in editor. Best for: Speech-to-Text platforms are a godsend for journalists, legal professionals, healthcare providers, and content creators who handle large volumes of audio data. They are equally beneficial for SMBs and large enterprises looking to improve meeting productivity and document internal knowledge. Accessibility teams also rely heavily on these tools to ensure compliance with ADA and other international accessibility standards. Not ideal for: These tools might not be necessary for casual users who only need to transcribe a few minutes of audio occasionally, as free built-in tools like Google Docs Voice Typing or Apple’s Dictation may suffice. They are also less ideal for highly sensitive, top-secret government discussions unless the platform offers on-premise deployment or extreme end-to-end encryption that meets specific national security standards. Top 10 Speech-to-Text (Transcription) Platforms 1 — Otter.ai Otter.ai has positioned itself as the go-to “meeting assistant” for the modern workforce. While it functions as a transcription tool, its primary design goal is to sit in on your Zoom, Google Meet, or Microsoft Teams calls and provide real-time, collaborative notes. Key features: OtterPilot: Automatically joins and records meetings even if you are late or absent. Real-time Transcription: Generates text as people speak, allowing users to highlight key points instantly. Automated Summaries: Uses AI to condense long meetings into a few bullet points and action items. Speaker Identification: Learns voices to accurately attribute dialogue in a multi-person conversation. Collaboration Tools: Allows team members to comment on and edit the transcript simultaneously. Advanced Search: Search through all past meetings for specific keywords or mentions. Direct Integration: Seamlessly syncs with calendars and video conferencing software. Pros: Exceptional for live meeting environments and collaborative work. The mobile app is highly polished, making it great for on-the-go recordings. Cons: Accuracy can dip significantly with heavy technical jargon or strong non-native accents. The free tier has become increasingly restrictive regarding monthly minute limits. Security & compliance: SSO, 256-bit AES encryption, SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, and CCPA compliant. Support & community: Robust help center, email-based customer support, and a large community of business users sharing best practices for remote work. 2 — Rev Rev is widely considered the gold standard for accuracy because it offers both AI-powered automated transcription and a network of over 70,000 human professionals who guarantee 99% accuracy. Key features: Human Transcription: High-accuracy transcripts handled by professional transcribers. ASR (AI) Transcription: A highly sophisticated proprietary AI for low-cost, fast drafts. Global Captions: Provides translated subtitles for videos in over 15 languages. Rev Max: A subscription service providing automated transcription and productivity tools. Interactive Editor: A web-based tool to sync audio with text for easy correction. Mobile Recorder App: Record audio directly on your phone and send it for transcription with one tap. API Access: Allows developers to integrate Rev’s transcription engine into their own apps. Pros: The 99% accuracy guarantee for human transcription is unmatched in the industry. Extremely fast turnaround times, often delivering human transcripts in under 12 hours. Cons: Human transcription is significantly more expensive than AI-only alternatives. The AI-only option, while good, can still struggle with complex audio compared to specialized niche tools. Security & compliance: SSO, data encryption at rest and in transit, HIPAA compliant, SOC 2 Type II, and GDPR compliant. Support & community: 24/7 customer support, extensive developer documentation, and a massive blog covering transcription and accessibility topics. 3 — Descript Descript has revolutionized the industry by treating audio and video editing like a text document. It is designed primarily for podcasters, YouTubers, and video marketers who want to edit their media by simply editing the transcript. Key features: Text-Based Editing: Deleting a word in the transcript automatically deletes that segment from the audio/video. Overdub: Create an AI clone of your voice to “type” in corrections for audio mistakes. Filler Word Removal: One-click removal of “ums,” “uhs,” and “likes.” Studio Sound: AI-driven noise cancellation that makes a phone recording sound like it was done in a studio. Multitrack Transcription: Keeps separate speakers on separate tracks for perfect clarity. Screen Recording: Integrated tool for creating tutorials and presentations with instant transcripts. Pros: The “edit-by-text” workflow is a massive time-saver for content creators. Overdub is a futuristic feature that can fix audio errors without rerecording. Cons: The learning curve can be steep for those used to traditional linear editors. Requires a significant amount of system resources (RAM/CPU) for the desktop app. Security & compliance: SSO, SOC 2 Type II, GDPR compliant, and data encryption. Support & community: Very active Discord community, “Descript Academy” tutorials, and responsive email support. 4 — Trint Trint is a premium transcription platform tailored specifically for journalists and media organizations that require high security and specialized editorial tools to turn raw audio into stories. Key features: Story Builder: Select highlights from multiple transcripts and assemble them into a script. Collaborative Editing: Real-time multi-user editing with “read-only” or “edit” permissions. Marker & Highlight Tools: Easy way to tag important quotes for quick retrieval. ISO-Certified Security: One of the few platforms with ISO 27001 certification. Mobile App: Record and upload directly from the field. Custom Vocabularies: Teach the AI specific names or industry terms to improve accuracy. Pros: Exceptionally clean interface designed for an editorial workflow. Top-tier security makes it suitable for sensitive investigative journalism. Cons: Pricing is high, making it less accessible for casual or solo users. AI accuracy is on par with others but lacks a human “safety net” option within the platform. Security & compliance: ISO 27001, SSO, GDPR compliant, SOC 2 Type II, and data encryption. Support & community: Enterprise-grade support, dedicated account managers for teams, and comprehensive onboarding documentation. 5 — Sonix Sonix is an automated transcription service that excels in its simplicity and its powerful multilingual capabilities, supporting over 40 languages with high precision. Key features: Multilingual Transcription: Supports 40+ languages and dialects. In-browser Editor: High-quality editor that highlights words with low confidence scores. Automated Translation: Translate your transcripts into dozens of languages within seconds. Custom Dictionary: Add specific technical terms to a global account dictionary. Word-by-word Timestamps: Perfect for SEO and deep data indexing. Direct Exports: Support for VTT, SRT, TXT, and PDF. Pros: Very fast processing times; a 1-hour file is often ready in less than 5 minutes. The translation engine is surprisingly accurate for business-level needs. Cons: Pay-as-you-go pricing can get expensive for heavy users compared to unlimited plans. Accuracy in languages other than English can vary depending on the dialect. Security & compliance: SSO, SOC 2 Type II, GDPR compliant, and 256-bit encryption. Support & community: Extensive help articles, email support, and a straightforward interface that rarely requires assistance. 6 — Happy Scribe Happy Scribe is a versatile platform popular among European businesses, offering a unique blend of AI and human-made transcription and subtitling services. Key features: AI & Human Hybrid: Choose between fast AI or high-accuracy human services. Advanced Subtitle Editor: Specialized tools for adjusting subtitle timing and aesthetics. Interactive Transcript Player: Embeddable player for websites to make audio content searchable. Collaboration Workspaces: Organize transcripts by project and team. No File Size Limit: Unlike some competitors, Happy Scribe handles massive video files easily. Pros: The subtitling tools are among the best for social media managers and filmmakers. Very strong performance with European languages and accents. Cons: Human services have a longer turnaround time than some US-based competitors. Some users find the organizational structure a bit clunky for very large accounts. Security & compliance: GDPR compliant (EU based), SSO, and data encryption. Support & community: Multilingual customer support, excellent user guides, and a highly-rated public roadmap. 7 — Verbit Verbit is an enterprise-level platform that uses a unique hybrid of AI and human editors to serve the legal, education, and media industries where compliance is critical. Key features: Sector-Specific AI: Specialized models for legal terminology and academic lectures. Live Captioning: Real-time captioning for live events and classrooms. Adaptive Learning: The AI learns from human corrections in real-time. LMS/CMS Integration: Built-in connectors for Blackboard, Canvas, and Kaltura. Compliance Workflows: Designed to meet ADA and Section 508 standards. Pros: The best choice for universities and law firms needing guaranteed accuracy and compliance. Seamless integration with educational technology ecosystems. Cons: Not designed for individuals or small startups; pricing is strictly enterprise. The platform can be overly complex for simple, one-off transcription needs. Security & compliance: HIPAA, SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, SSO, and ISO 27001. Support & community: Dedicated customer success managers, 24/7 technical support, and comprehensive onboarding. 8 — Scribie Scribie is a veteran in the transcription space, focusing on a multi-step human review process to ensure high-fidelity transcripts at a very competitive price point. Key features: Four-Step Process: Every file goes through transcription, review, proofreading, and quality check. Strict Confidentiality: Transcribers only see small segments of audio to protect privacy. Free Automated Draft: Every order comes with a free AI-generated transcript first. Detailed Speaker Tracking: Precise identification even in crowded room environments. Standard/Clean Verbatim: Choose whether to include or exclude “umms” and stutters. Pros: One of the most affordable ways to get high-accuracy human transcription. The segmented transcription process adds a unique layer of privacy. Cons: The web interface feels dated compared to modern AI platforms. Turnaround times can be slower during peak periods. Security & compliance: SSO, data encryption, and GDPR compliant. Support & community: Reliable email and phone support, though less “community-driven” than newer apps. 9 — Temi Temi is a “no-frills” automated transcription service owned by the same parent company as Rev. It is designed for those who want a fast, cheap, and simple transcript without any extra fluff. Key features: Simple Upload: Drag and drop interface for immediate processing. Confidence Scores: Highlights words the AI isn’t sure about. Timestamping: Included on every paragraph for easy navigation. Basic Editor: Simple web-based tool to make quick corrections. Mobile App: Basic recording and ordering functionality. Pros: Probably the easiest-to-use tool on this list for beginners. Highly predictable, low-cost pricing. Cons: Lacks advanced features like collaboration, AI summaries, or voice cloning. Accuracy is strictly tied to audio quality; it has no human backup option. Security & compliance: Data encryption and GDPR compliant. Support & community: Online help center and email support. 10 — Dragon Professional (Nuance) Dragon Professional is the industry leader for desktop dictation. Unlike web platforms, this software lives on your computer and is designed for users who want to “write” documents and control their PC using their voice. Key features: Deep Dictation: Real-time speech-to-text directly into Microsoft Word, Outlook, and more. Voice Commands: Control your entire computer (menus, clicking, typing) via voice. Industry Editions: Specialized versions for Legal and Medical (Dragon Medical One). On-device Processing: Does not require an active internet connection for basic dictation. Custom Macros: Create voice commands to insert long blocks of text or perform tasks. Pros: The most powerful tool for individuals with accessibility needs or repetitive strain injuries. Extreme accuracy once it learns an individual’s specific voice pattern. Cons: Expensive upfront software cost compared to monthly subscriptions. Primarily focused on a single speaker (dictation) rather than multi-speaker interviews. Security & compliance: ISO 27001, HIPAA (Medical edition), GDPR, and local data storage. Support & community: Professional training available, certified partner network, and massive enterprise support infrastructure. Choosing a transcription tool is not about finding the “objectively best” software, but the one that aligns with your specific workflow. Solo Users vs SMB vs Mid-market vs Enterprise Solo Users: If you just need transcripts for your own use, Otter.ai or Temi offer the best price-to-performance ratio. SMBs: Content creation teams will find Descript or Happy Scribe invaluable for repurposing media. Mid-Market: Organizations needing collaboration and high-volume management should look toward Trint or the team plans of Otter. Enterprise: For legal, medical, or higher-ed compliance, Verbit or Rev’s enterprise solutions are the only safe choices. Budget-conscious vs Premium Solutions If you have a zero or low budget, Otter’s free tier or Temi’s low per-minute rate are ideal. However, if accuracy is paramount and you cannot afford to spend time proofreading, paying the premium for Rev’s human transcription is a worthwhile investment. With AI dubbing, content can be automatically generated and translated into the target language. The software offers advanced tools to clone the speaker’s voice and generate new speech in the target language. Video translation software also enhances the quality of the dubbed video with features like multi-track recording, synchronization tools, pitch adjustments, and more. Many video translation tools offer pre-recorded libraries of different languages and accents. Video translation software differs from localization software in some ways. While video translation software replaces the original audio with a different language, localization software adapts content for different languages and cultures by understanding various dialects, references, and contexts and helping content resonate with the target audience. AI video generation also differs from video translation software in many ways, one of which is generating the entire piece of content using machine learning models. Show activity on this post. Certainly under Xenial Xerus you have access to a quite reasonable copy of FFmpeg so the resize can be handled easily with FFmpeg from the command line. Definitions: First some definitions to solve the endless confusion over terminology: 720p: Has a vertical resolution of 720 pixels, horizontal resolution usually of 1280px. Aspect ratio is most usually 16:9. The 'p' simply stands for progressive scan, i.e. non-interlaced. 480p: Has a vertical resolution of 480 pixels, horizontal resolution usually of 640 pixels. Aspect ratio is most usually 4:3. Again the 'p' stands for progressive scan, i.e. non-interlaced. Required Software: The great news is that FFmpeg will do the calculations for the horizontal resolution for you as well as maintaining the required aspect ratio, it is only required for you to give the desired vertical resolution. So first install FFmpeg: sudo apt-get install ffmpeg libavcodec-extra The libavcodec-extra package will install some often-needed extra codecs for FFmpeg. The 'Resize' Syntax: The basic syntax to resize your video is as follows: ffmpeg -i input -vf scale=-1:480 output The scale filter uses width:height and you can see in my example that I have specified a height (vertical resolution) of 480 while the '-1' tells FFmpeg to resize the width (horizontal resolution) as necessary to maintain the existing aspect ratio. Pretty cool :). A Full Example: Bear in mind that you will need to also re-encode when you are resizing and your selected settings will depend very much on your source material. To give an example: Resize the video stream to 480p and export as an H.264 stream Copy the audio stream For this use the following command line: ffmpeg -i input.mp4 \ -vf scale=-2:480 -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 22 \ -c:a copy output.mp4 Note that I have specified -2:480 for width and height, this allows FFmpeg to calculate a number for width that is divisible by 2 which will give more efficient encoding. There is a great deal more to scaling with FFmpeg, I have included a reference at the base if you wish to dig a little deeper... content: CookiesWe use cookies to improve your experience and analyze traffic. Customize your preferences to control how your information is handled.网站翻译2025年你可以尝试的最佳机器翻译软件作者Merve Alsan审阅人更新于2025 年 12 月 19 日2025 年 12 月 19 日说到文本翻译，现在企业除了找人工翻译，还有一个靠谱的选择：那就是用机器翻译软件。机器翻译软件（也叫MT软件）是一种基于人工智能的工具，能自动翻译不同语言之间的文本，比如从英语到西班牙语，反之亦然。虽然机器翻译软件刚出现的时候，翻译准确性可能没那么高，但几十年来技术不断进步，现在它已经能做得相当准确了。因此，这类软件经常被整合到计算机辅助翻译（CAT）工具里，供那些有国际项目的企业使用。比如，想要把网页本地化的国际企业，就可以用机器翻译软件来大规模翻译大量文本。不过，MT软件可不只是用来翻译网站的。它还能翻译那些对维护成功的国际商业关系很重要的文件。 投资翻译带来的经济效益是显而易见的：根据Common Sense Advisory（现在叫CSA Research）的一项调查，那些在翻译上投入更多的财富500强企业，报告总收入增长的可能性要比没有投入的企业高出1.5倍。接下来，我们会带你了解那些顶级的机器翻译软件，对比它们的优点和局限性，还会告诉你怎么才能有效地为你的业务做好网站翻译。注意：想找个工具来翻译你的网站吗？试试 Weglot 的14天免费试用吧，看看你如何利用AI网站翻译来快速上线一个多语言网站。 为什么网站翻译软件这么重要？市场上一些大公司之所以把翻译看得这么重要，并且都用翻译软件来做，那是有原因的：因为这能赚钱啊。首先，尽管52%的网站都是英文的，但以英语为母语的人口在全球总人口中只占不到5%。这说明很多网站都错过了那些能带来利润的市场。 这是因为，虽然互联网上的内容大多是为英语用户准备的，但消费者在用母语浏览的网站上购买东西的可能性，要高出73%。 大公司都明白这个道理。比如，微软已经把自己的产品翻译成了90多种语言，东芝翻译了30多种，苹果也翻译了40种。从长远来看，翻译你的网站不仅能提高销售额，还能提升你的营销效果，比如SEO（搜索引擎优化）。 超过一半的Google搜索都不是英文的，所以如果你不为目标受众的母语创建内容，又怎么能超越国际竞争对手呢？ 答案是：你做不到。这时候，机器翻译软件就派上用场了。机器翻译能帮你把网站本地化，还能提升多语言SEO（搜索引擎优化），这样就能扩大你的市场范围了。 这是因为，当非英语访客用母语阅读内容时，他们会更愿意和你的网站互动。超过56%的消费者都说过，用自己的语言获取信息比价格更重要。 尽管大多数现代浏览器都自带了和常用在线翻译器（它们也用了先进的机器翻译系统）整合的功能，但母语使用者会觉得更自在，因为他们知道网站内容是一开始就用他们的语言呈现的，而不是需要自己手动用翻译App把外语文本翻译过来。就拿respond.io来说吧。这个客户对话管理平台用 Weglot 把他们的网站翻译成了十五种新语言。用了这个方案以后，网站的流量和曝光量都翻了2倍。既然 respond.io 能有这样的好成绩，你当然也能享受到类似的效果啦！机器翻译在2025年及未来的发展趋势 说实话，机器翻译刚出来的时候，效果确实不怎么样。1950年代：第一个机器翻译系统诞生。1970年代：语音识别技术开始发展。1980年代：电子词典和术语数据库出现。1990年代：统计机器翻译和计算机辅助翻译工具问世。2006年：谷歌翻译上线。2016年：谷歌引入神经网络机器翻译。机器翻译最早的尝试是在1950年代开始的，那时的系统主要依靠基于规则的机器翻译（RBMT）。到了1970年代，RBMT技术已经很成熟了，它会用一套语法规则和双语词典来翻译文本。不过，这些系统常常会给出很直白或生硬的翻译，因为它们很难处理语言里那些细微的差别。结果，机器翻译几乎立刻就“名声不好”了。人们觉得机器翻译的准确率太低，很不满意，就开始觉得它不如“专业”（也就是人工）翻译，所以更愿意选择网站翻译服务来处理自己的内容。从基于规则的机器翻译到统计机器翻译幸运的是，对于机器翻译提供商来说，随着技术的发展，机器翻译开始摆脱负面形象。在RBMT之后，出现了统计机器翻译（SMT），它通过分析现有的人工翻译（也就是双语语料库）来翻译文本。然后，它会使用预测算法来判断在特定情况下文本的最佳翻译方式。SMT相对于RBMT来说是一个很大的进步，但有时准确性还是不够。不过，发展并没有止步于此。如今，最新、最棒的机器翻译技术是神经网络机器翻译（NMT），它利用复杂的深度学习模型来翻译文本。神经网络机器翻译登场神经网络机器翻译（NMT）借助复杂的语言翻译算法，能够生成高质量的翻译。这些翻译不仅更准确，而且听起来更自然，比RMBT和SMT技术产生的翻译要好很多。如今，NMT的强大效果已经平息了大部分对机器翻译的反对声音。甚至连“机器翻译不能识别或翻译图片和PPT幻灯片里的文字！”这样的异议，也基本销声匿迹了——因为先进的机器翻译工具完全可以做到这一点。生成式AI：会是机器翻译软件的未来吗？ 2022-2023年，大型语言模型（LLMs）和生成式AI的出现，给机器翻译带来了很多新的可能。和传统的NMT系统不一样，那些系统是专门针对两种语言之间的翻译来训练的，而生成式AI模型是在海量的多语言数据上训练出来的，所以它们能更全面地理解不同语言之间的语境。这些AI模型在处理那些细致入微的翻译时，展现出了很大的潜力。比如，它们能搞定习语、文化典故，以及那些传统上机器翻译很难处理的、和语境相关的意思。举个例子，它们通常能在比较长的文本里保持语调和风格的一致性，有些甚至还能根据特定的行业或受众来调整翻译。不过，要记住，生成式AI并不会完全取代NMT。相反，许多翻译服务商正在探索混合方法，把这两种技术的优点结合起来。这种结合有望带来传统NMT的可靠性和效率，同时拥有生成式AI的语境理解和适应能力。你的公司应该使用机器翻译软件吗？ 机器翻译现在在市场上被广泛使用，对于需要以最有效率的方式获得持续准确翻译的国际企业来说，简直是救星。就连专业翻译人员也会采用自动化翻译技术来简化和加快翻译过程呢！但为什么呢？下面是机器翻译软件的一些好处，你的公司也能享受到哦：操作简单：机器翻译软件操作起来非常简单，你不需要有技术背景也能像专业人士一样使用它。启动软件，复制粘贴你的原文，设置目标语言，就能实时获得翻译好的文本。速度更快：机器翻译软件可以在几秒钟内完成文本翻译，而人工翻译可能需要几个小时甚至几天，这取决于文本量的大小。 content: Viewing captions in another language Viewing captions in another language English (Original) English (Original)日本語 This article was updated • 2025-09-17 Copy Permalink In this article RequirementsHow to view translated captions Enable captions in a meeting or webinarChange the speaking language for captionsTranslate captions into another languageView full transcriptAdjust closed captioning size Supported languages for translated captions Zoom translated captions enable users to have the speech in a meeting or webinar automatically translated in real-time to captions in another language. For example, if the speaker is speaking English in a meeting, captions can be made available in Spanish, Chinese, Ukrainian, and more. Available caption languages are determined by the host in web settings before the live session, but participants can freely enable captions and select the language they want to use for translation without the need of the host. Requirements for viewing translated captions Zoom desktop app for Windows or macOS: Global minimum version or higherZoom web appAutomated captions and translated captions enabled* *Note: Translated captioning requires the host to be a member of a Zoom Workplace Business Plus, Zoom Workplace Enterprise Essentials, Zoom Workplace Enterprise Plus, or Zoom Workplace Enterprise Premier account, or assigned the Zoom Translated Captions add-on Show more How to view translated captions Enable captions in a meeting or webinar Any participant in the meeting or webinar can self-enable captions, as they are not dependent on the host to enable. Join a Zoom meeting or webinar.In the meeting controls toolbar, click the Show Captions icon .Note: You may have to click More, then click Captions.Captions will appear above the controls toolbar. By default, English is set as the speaking language the captions are generated in. Note: Users can also have the Zoom desktop app automatically show captions, when available in the meeting or webinar. Change the speaking language for captions If the speaker is presenting in another language, that speaker can change the language the captions are generated from. By default, English is set as the speaking language the captions are generated from. If you are presenting in another language, for example French, you can change input language so that captions are generated accurately in French. Next to the Show Captions icon, click the up arrow icon .Click the Caption language: English menu and select the appropriate language the captions should be generated from.Once selected, captions will be generated based on the language chosen. Notes: This only changes the language the captions should be generated from. This does not provide a translation into another language other than what the presenter is speaking.Choice of Speaking Language will be saved and applied to future meetings. Translate captions into another language If the speaker is presenting in another language and you want the captions to be generated into your language, Zoom can translate the captions into your preferred language. This is done in real-time during the meeting, and can be set by each individual participant. Language pairs (the input speaking language and the output caption language) available to participants are determined by the host’s settings. Next to the Show Captions icon, click the up arrow icon .Under Captions and translation, enable Translation, and select the language you want the captions translated to.Click Save.Once a different language is chosen, the captions will be generated and translated into that language for you. Other participants can choose a language for their captions independently of your chosen language. Note: Choice of Translate to language will be saved and applied to future meetings. View full transcript You can view a full transcription of your meeting or webinar if live transcription is enabled. In the meeting controls, next to the Show Captions icon, click the up arrow icon .Under Captions and translation, click View full transcript. The Transcript panel will appear, displaying the meeting's or webinar's full transcript.(Optional) In the Transcript panel, click the Pop out icon to detach the transcript panel on a separate window. Click the Pop in icon to attach the transcript panel back to the main Zoom desktop app.(Optional) At the bottom of the Transcript panel, click Save Transcript to save a file of the full transcript.(Optional) Use the search bar to search through the transcript.(Optional) To hide the full transcript: In the meeting controls: Next to the Show Captions icon, click the up arrow icon .Under Captions and translation, click Close Full Transcript. In the Transcript panel: In the top right corner, click the X icon to close the transcript window. Adjust closed captioning size In the meeting controls, next to the Show Captions icon, click the up arrow icon .Under Captions and translation, click Caption settings. The Accessibility desktop app settings window will appear.Under Closed captioning, move the slider to adjust the caption font size . After being in the interpreting field since 2007, I have seen our area change and expand. Boostlingo is allowing our agency to become a commanding force within the market. With the assistance of our account manager & Boost’s developer, I have been able to see changes I wish for become reality. As an interpreting organization, we can set permissions, rates, and specialties. We have quick access to interpreter email addresses and phone numbers, and we can download a file of our interpreter’s information. Telephonic service can be accessed by a mobile app, by accessing video/audio on a computer, or by dialing in to a phone number. Each avenue of connection allows our agency to gather important data, to ensure accurate invoicing for our accounts. As Boostlingo grows, their developers have allowed for a unique level of personalization for each calling account. Using the app and website, our accounts access ASL interpreters to help remain ADA compliant, and language access provides Title VI compliance. There is a fully integrated invoicing system built into their website, which can work in conjunction with QuickBooks. Personalization options allow us to use a domain that features our own logo and color scheme choice. Our organization has an account manager who listens intently to any feedback I have. With global level of changes and settings, smaller personalization is not always possible. For example, we can add our logo to the interpreter’s printable form, but we cannot change the way the information prints or the size of the font it prints with. The digital signature, as it is currently, won’t work for us, so we stick with printed forms. We struggle with account rates - it feels like it is too smart, so we are finding ways to work around it. Billing reports cannot be customized as much as we would like, especially to meet contractual obligations when invoicing. The biggest speed bump we found is the account set up must either be completed by Boost support or by someone at the account organization that is willing to set up access.
